Guided by Social Cognitive Theory, this qualitative study examined semi-structured interviews with 36 undergraduate chemistry students from 22 higher education institutions in China. Thematic analysis identified interrelated personal, behavioral, and environmental influences.

title: In Silico Design and Structural Validation ofEpitope-Based Vaccine Candidates Against Feline Calicivirus using Immunoinformatics
abstract: This research aims to utilize bioinformatics methods to identify and analyze potential vaccine epitopes for feline calicivirus (FCV). FCV is a highly contagious pathogen causing respiratory illnesses in cats, posing significant challenges due to its genetic variability. The project involved retrieving FCV nucleotide sequences, predicting potential vaccine epitopes, and evaluating their antigenicity, toxicity, and allergenicity. The properties of the vaccine peptide sequence were also predicted and analyzed in 3D.

title: Vibronic Absorption and Circular Dichroism Spectra of Chiral PDI Aggregates in Free Space and Optical Cavities
abstract: Manipulating molecular chirality via strong light–matter coupling holds promise for asymmetric photochemistry and chiral optoelectronics, but a microscopic understanding of how cavity confinement, excitonic delocalization, and vibronic coupling intertwine is still lacking. We address this by simulating the polaritonic absorption and CD spectra of helical perylenediimide (PDI) aggregates in optical cavities, using a generalized Holstein–Tavis–Cummings (HTC) model parametrized from ab initioelectronic-structure calculations and solved with the non-Markovian stochastic Schrödinger equation…

title: Pocket and ligand embeddings for 72,199 protein–ligand complexes from the Protein Data Bank
abstract: This work presents a retrieval resource covering 72,199 protein–ligand complexes from the Protein Data Bank. Each complex carries a 1,280-dimensional pocket embedding, obtained by mean-pooling final-layer ESM-2 representations over binding-site residues within 8 Å of the ligand and computed per chain rather than over a concatenation of all polymer chains; a 2,048-bit RDKit Morgan fingerprint of the ligand, taken from the idealized Chemical Component Dictionary entry and therefore shared by complexes binding the same component (26,619 distinct fingerprints across the 72,199 rows); and HDF5…

title: A Latent Ability Model for Benchmarking Molecular Representations
abstract: The growing number of chemical foundation models calls for a standardized benchmarking method both for practitioners choosing representations and researchers identifying gaps. Previous work that ranked latent abilities of various chemical embeddings to predict ADMET properties suffered from significant shortcomings, including the use of biased datasets incongruent with real world usage and overstating statistically significant differences in model performance.

title: From Boron Flatland to 3D Pharmacophore Space: Tacn-Supported Boronium Cage Cations
abstract: Replacement of C–C bonds with isoelectronic B–N units offers a compelling yet underdeveloped strategy for modulating molecular structure and electronic properties. Here we report that tacn-family ligands (1,4,7-triazacyclononane and its N-alkyl derivatives) enable the straightforward assembly of polycyclic boronium(+2) cations through a simple one-pot reaction with Me 2 SBHBr 2 under ambient conditions. These reactions produce rigid cage structures in which three fused five-membered rings are formed in a single step via tridentate coordination of the ligand to a [BH] 2+ core.

title: EnGOAT: An Energy–Geometry Analysis Toolkit for Free-Energy Surfaces of Mobile Species in Crystalline Materials
abstract: The free-energy surface (FES) of a mobile species in a crystalline host governs its behavior within the material, including properties such as adsorption and transport, but reducing it to quantitative descriptors remains challenging. We present the Energy–GeOmetry Analysis Toolkit (EnGOAT), an open-source framework for the energetic, geometric, and topological analysis of volumetric FES data.

title: Decision Framework for Polymer Composite Linings in Trenchless Renewal: Integrating Materials Durability, Operational Performance, Application Quality, and Environmental Sustainability
abstract: Polymer composite linings are increasingly used in trenchless renewal technologies. These technologies are advantageous when material durability, structural requirements, application quality and service exposure are considered together, yet renewal decisions are still made largely case by case, often overlooking some of these aspects. This paper develops an evidence-based decision framework in which every decision rule is an explicit, traceable statement linked to measured or published evidence.

title: Closed-loop formulation–process optimization under unknown feasibility for extended-release pellets
abstract: Pharmaceutical formulation development frequently encounters formulation–process conditions that fail before a viable product is produced, leaving downstream performance unobservable and experimental feasibility unknown a priori. Here, we demonstrate a closed-loop formulation-development workflow that jointly optimizes formulation and process variables while learning experimental feasibility from physical outcomes.

title: Correlation-Energy Extrapolation within Shell-Nested Virtual Spaces
abstract: We show that power-law extrapolation of the correlation energy can be carried from a sequence of orbital bases into a shell hierarchy within one molecular virtual space. In shell-nested virtual spaces (SNVS), atomic natural orbitals guide the radial and angular content of successive layers, and the correlating-orbital count beyond the valence-virtual space replaces the cardinal number in a two-point formula. The construction uses one Hartree–Fock reference in one parent basis.

title: Structure Determination of Surface Sites in Heterogeneous Olefin Metathesis Catalysts from 95Mo NMR Signatures
abstract: Heterogeneous olefin metathesis catalysts composed of highly dispersed Mo sites on support carriers are used to produce key olefin building blocks for higher value-added products, e.g. the Shell Higher Olefin Process (SHOP). However, understanding the nature of Mo sites in catalysts, i.e. molybdenum oxides supported on amorphous supports like silica, MoOx/SiO2, is hampered by a low fraction of surface metal sites (low loading), the possible distribution of surface species and the lack of very sensitive characterization methods to distinguish subtle changes in the coordination environment of…

title: Uncovering Heterogeneous Energetic Trajectories in NiFe Oxygen Evolution Electrocatalysis through Integrated Raman, Electrochemical and Microkinetic Analysis
abstract: Fe incorporation strongly modifies the activity of Ni-based electrocatalysts, but how heterogeneous surface states contribute to this behavior remain unclear due to improper understanding about intermediate evolution. Here, we investigate whether correlations between spatially resolved spectroscopic features and electrochemical responses can reveal distinct energetic and kinetic characteristics of NiFe electrodes. We combine in-situ Raman mapping, electrochemistry and microkinetic modeling to study three NiFe electrodes prepared under different Fe-deposition conditions.

title: Scalable Density-Based Bootstrap Embedding with Perturbative Triples for Large Molecular Systems
abstract: Extending density-based bootstrap embedding (BE) with perturbative triples to large molecules requires control of both fragment solver cost and tensor storage. We present a restricted and unrestricted BE-CCSD(T) implementation combining density-fitted embedding transformations, fragment parallelism, and streamed contractions of triples density contributions. Explicit one-and two-particle terms and the correction to the coupled-cluster multipliers are retained without assembling a molecular two-particle density matrix or storing a complete triples tensor.

title: Reproducibility, Benchmarks, and Mechanistic Diversity: Building Trust in Computational Electrocatalysis for the AI Era
abstract: Computational electrocatalysis has contributed significantly to the design of electrocatalysts for energy conversion and storage. Yet three avoidable shortcomings constrain the reliability and reusability of computational results: incomplete reporting, oversimplification of reaction pathways and/or active sites considered, and inconsistent protocols for constructing free-energy changes (ΔG). Researchers may therefore be forced to repeat calculations simply to recover structures, verify reference conventions, or identify the source of conflicting results.

title: Modular Synthesis of N-Heterocycle-Substituted α-Amino Esters
abstract: Rapid analogue generation is central to early-stage drug discovery, creating demand for synthetic methods that combine modularity, operational simplicity, and broad substrate compatibility. N-Heterocyclesubstituted α-amino carbonyls are poorly served in this respect, their synthesis largely depending on a narrow pool of commercially available α-halogenated carbonyls.

title: Direct Determination of Pyroelectric Coefficients in Molecular Crystals by X-ray Quantum Crystallography
abstract: Organic molecular crystals with piezoelectric and pyroelectric responses are emerging as soft, biocompatible materials for next-generation energy harvesting. However, quantifying crystal polarity in such materials—and its variations under mechanical or thermal stimuli—on a structural basis remains challenging. Here, we estimate pyroelectric coefficients directly from high-resolution X-ray quantum crystallography (QCr) via accurate modelling of hydrogen positions and electron densities.

title: Combining Chemical Protein Synthesis and Cell Delivery for Photoproximity Labeling in Living Cells
abstract: Mapping a protein’s local environment is essential for understanding its cellular roles. Proximity labeling (PL) identifies nearby proteins, while photoproximity labeling (PPL) adds temporal control through light activation. However, intracellular applications of these methods commonly rely on genetically encoded fusions that could alter protein localization or function and offer limited control over defined, site-specific post-translational modifications (PTMs).

title: How to Discover New Electrolyte Additives for Lithium Batteries: A Computational Roadmap
abstract: Electrolyte additives, present at a few weight percent or less, decide whether a lithium battery forms a stable solidelectrolyte interphase, survives high-voltage operation, tolerates trace water and HF, or resists fire. For three decades most additives were found by trial and error, and the few design rules that emerged, most famously “a lower LUMO than the solvent”, were known to fail almost as soon as they were formulated.

title: Scaled-Up Production of Graphene Oxide: Design, Simulation, and Analysis of a Stirred Tank Batch Reactor
abstract: Graphene oxide (GO) is an emerging product experiencing exponential growth in popularity and demand. This comprehensive research evaluates the technical and economic feasibility of implementing a large-scale GO production plant in Malaysia, based on existing pilot-scale data from the industry. The major aspect of the GO production process is the GO synthesis reaction, carried out in a jacketed, stirred tank batch reactor of approximately 500 L capacity.
authors: Abu Danish Aiman Bin Abu Sofian

title: DEL-Flow: AI-Driven Structural Generation and Activity Validation of MDM2-Targeting Macrocyclic Peptides
abstract: Macrocyclic peptides represent a promising modality for modulating intracellular protein–protein interactions; however, macrocyclic peptide datasets with reliable experimental activity measurements that can inform rational design remain limited. Here, we developed DEL-Flow, a pocket-conditioned generative framework for the design of MDM2-p53 inhibitors. Using an iterative DEL-selection strategy, a first-generation symmetric dimeric macrocyclic peptide DEL identified a half-scaffold associated with highly enriched library members, which was retained to construct a second-generation asymmetric…

title: Cross-Validation of Electrochemical, Spectroscopic, and Gravimetric Methods for Characterizing Self-Assembled Monolayers
abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are widely used to tune the properties of metal electrode surfaces, with applications ranging from sensing to electrocatalysis. However, the structure, coverage, and stability of SAMs often evolve under applied potential, and no single experimental technique provides a complete description of these changes. This work demonstrates the application of several surface characterization techniques, including voltammetric, spectroscopic, and gravimetric methods, on a model SAM system comprised of 4-mercaptobenzonitrile (4-MBN) on a gold electrode.

title: Synthesis of Benzothieno[3,2-b]benzothiophene Propellanes via [2 + 2] Photocycloadditions through Energy Transfer Process
abstract: Propellanes are molecules with unique three-dimensional (3D) structures and chemical properties. Owing to their strained and rigid molecular frameworks, propellanes have attracted considerable attention in various fields. Heteroacenes, such as benzothieno[3,2-b]benzothiophene (BTBT), are widely used in materials science. However, there are few reports on the synthesis of heteroacene-derived propellanes.

title: Enantioselective intramolecular 1,3-diamination of acrylates
abstract: The enantioselective synthesis of bicyclic dihydrouracil and sulfamide derivatives through an intramolecular 1,3-diamination of acrylates is described. The method relies on the cyclization of urea and bis-sulfamide substrates, bearing a remote conjugated p-nitrophenyl ester, in the presence of a chiral isothiourea catalyst and diphenyl phosphate as an acid additive, affording the corresponding bicyclic products in good yields (up to 97%) and with excellent enantioselectivities (typically 94:6-97:3, up to 99.5:0.5 er).

title: Metastable hydrate of sodium chloride is a pentahydrate as revealed by 3D electron diffraction
abstract: ABSTRACT: Mixtures of water and NaCl, the archetypal salt, play important roles in industrial processes and natural environments on Earth and throughout the Solar System, yet their structural diversity at low temperatures remains poorly understood. Here, we determine the crystal structure of the metastable sodium chloride hydrate formed upon flash freezing using three-dimensional electron diffraction.

title: Lewis Base-Induced Valence Tautomerism in a Phosphorus Cation Enables the Activation of Strong Element-Fluorine Bonds
abstract: Main-group compounds show drastic differences in properties and reactivity between their n and n+2 oxidation states. While this often precludes transition-metal mimetic redox catalysis, precise control over prevalent oxidation states in a switchable compound could offer promising avenues for main-group-mediated processes. We demonstrate that hypercoordination-induced valence tautomerism unlocks high effective Lewis acidity in a phosphorus cation.

title: Achieving Accurate Prediction of Water Adsorption in Mildly Hydrophobic MOFs
abstract: Accurately predicting the steep, S-shaped water adsorption isotherms of mildly hydrophobic MOFs and other hydrophobic porous materials remains challenging. This difficulty stems from the delicate balance between framework–water and water–water interactions that governs cooperative pore filling. Here, we develop a machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP), trained on reliable density functional theory reference data, for the prototypical mildly hydrophobic channel MOF MIP-211(Al).

title: A Boomerang Catalyst Combining High Catalytic Activity and Reusability for Aqueous Transfer Hydrogenation of Ketones
abstract: We report a boomerang-type iridium catalyst that combines the high activity of homogeneous catalysis with spontaneous and quantitative catalyst recovery without external operation. The catalyst consists of a Cp*Ir complex immobilized on a cross-linked poly(acrylic acid) gel (PAA). Upon addition of formic acid (FA), Ir species are released into solution, enabling the aqueous transfer hydrogenation of a broad range of ketones under air without additional additives. In situ analyses confirmed the presence of soluble Cp*Ir reaction intermediates during the reaction.

title: A Machine Learning Approach to logBB Prediction Combining Molecular Docking and Quantum-Chemical Descriptors
abstract: Blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability is a major challenge in the development of drugs targeting the central nervous system (CNS). Computational prediction methods can help prioritize candidate compounds and reduce the experimental workload during early drug discovery. In this study, machine learning models were developed to predict the blood-to-brain concentration ratio expressed as its decimal logarithm (logBB).

title: Chitosan as a Sustainable Loading-Density-Tunable Scaffold for Switching Energy- and Electron-Transfer Pathways in Porphyrin Photocatalysis
abstract: Support architectures critically govern the molecular organization and excited-state pathways of organic chromophores. Chitosan, one of the most widely studied sustainable, biomass-derived polysaccharides, has typically served as a low-loading, aggregation-suppressing host for photofunctional chromophores such as porphyrins. By contrast, high chromophore loading remains largely unexplored because it is generally assumed to cause detrimental aggregation-induced quenching.

title: Geometric Reaction Path Alignment for Kinetic Feasibility Assessment
abstract: Automated reaction exploration can generate more candidate elementary steps than can be practically characterized with transition-state searches. Thermodynamic screening provides an inexpensive first filter, but endpoint energies contain no information about the path connecting reactants and products. Here, we introduce SPARTA (Steric Path Alignment for Reactive Transformation Assessment), a geometric kinetic proxy that generates reaction-biased endpoint conformers, refines them through iterative image-dependent pair potential path optimization, and evaluates electronic single-point energies…

title: Tailoring Chain-Edge C=R (R = C, O, S) Microenvironments in sp2-Carbon-Bridged 1D COFs Unlocks a ‘Moderate Balance’ Effect for Photocatalytic H2O2 Production
abstract: One-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (1D COFs) featuring double-chain architectures offer abundant exposed active sites for photocatalysis. However, topological constraints and entropy-driven stacking disorder severely impede their controllable synthesis, obscuring definitive structure–activity relationships. Herein, we report a series of sp2-carbon-bridged 1D COFs with atomically tailored chain-edge microenvironments (C=R-COFs, R = C, O, S) for efficient photocatalytic H2O2 production.

title: Adsorbate Resonance-Assisted Hydrogen Bonding across Solid Interfaces
abstract: In this work, we identify and characterize a cooperative interaction between adsorbates in which hydrogen bonding and surface-mediated bond redistribution reinforce one another across a solid interface. We show that this phenomenon, which we term adsorbate resonance-assisted hydrogen bonding (ARAHB), arises from the transfer of covalent bond character along a hydrogen-bond coordinate, coupled to bond redistribution throughout the adsorbate-surface complex. We develop a computational workflow to test and identify ARAHB among coadsorbates.

title: The Limited Contribution of Structural Information Relative to Language-Model Signal in Data-Limited Cryptic Pocket Prediction
abstract: Cryptic pockets, drug-binding sites absent from a protein’s static structure but exposed through conformational change, expand the scope of druggable targets, yet remain difficult to identify computationally. PocketMiner, a structure-based graph neural network trained on molecular dynamics simulation data, predicts cryptic pocket formation from a single static structure (ROC-AUC 0.87).

title: Critical Evaluation of Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy for State-of-Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Cells Against Battery Management System Baselines
abstract: Machine-learning models that estimate the state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion cells from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) are rarely compared with models using only data a battery management system (BMS) records. Of 30 audited studies using three public datasets, one reported such a baseline. With whole cells held out, impedance brought no detectable gain over the strongest baseline on two exploratory datasets.

title: Normalized Nucleic Acid Payload in Lipid Nanoparticles: A Perspective on the Harmonization of Published Data
abstract: Precise and consistent reporting of the nucleic acid payload per lipid nanoparticle (LNP) is important for advancing the understanding and development of nanomedicines. However, the reported number of RNA molecules ranges between ∼1-300 in recent investigations. To evaluate the RNA payload across investigations, we introduce and apply a normalized nucleic acid payload metric which accounts for differences in LNP size, nucleotides per RNA and N/P charge ratio.

title: Intermolecular Hydrogen-Bond Preorganization Enables Concerted 2e−/2H+ Transfer in the Franck–Condon Region
abstract: Concerted proton-coupled electron transfer (CPET) is central to biological and synthetic energy conversion, yet most studies focus on 1e−/1H+ reactions. The principles governing concerted multi‑proton multi‑electron transfer, as illustrated by water oxidation and CO2 reduction, remain poorly understood. Here, we use femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy to investigate a water-soluble fluoflavine. Following photoexcitation, we resolve an ultrafast branching (<120 fs) from the Franck‑Condon region.

title: Comprehensive Profiling of Microcystins in Non-Targeted LC-HR-MS Datasets using Mass Spectrometry Query Language (MassQL)
abstract: Microcystins (MC) are a critical class of toxic cyanobacterial secondary metabolites, with specific variants such as MC-LR strictly regulated in drinking water. Despite their extensive structural diversity, comprising over 300 known congeners, comprehensive environmental monitoring is severely hindered by the limited availability of commercial reference standards and public tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) spectra.

title: Massively parallel quantification and prediction of monomeric protein yield in Escherichia coli
abstract: Obtaining sufficient quantities of purified proteins in their intended molecular states is essential for biological research and protein engineering. Advances in computational protein design have expanded the functional capabilities of de novo proteins and accelerated candidate generation. However, reliable methods for ranking expected monomeric yield of candidate de novo designs, including molecular binders, fluorescent proteins and enzymes, have yet to be established. Standardized measurements of monomeric yield across diverse sequences remain scarce, limiting our understanding of its determinants and the development of accurate predictors for candidate selection. Here we developed a scalable pooled assay combining peptide barcodes, size-exclusion chromatography and mass spectrometry to quantify monomeric yield for over 39,000 natural protein domain variants, de novo proteins and nanobodies under uniform and standardized Escherichia coli production conditions. We used this dataset to (1) quantify the relationship between folding stability and monomeric yield, (2) benchmark inverse-folding methods, (3) evaluate the utility of structure-prediction confidence metrics in selecting high-yield design candidates, and (4) identify sequence and structural patterns in nanobodies associated with monomeric yield and monomer-to-dimer yield ratios. We further developed ESMC-MonoYield, a protein language model fine-tuned to predict monomeric yield from amino acid sequence alone, and prospectively demonstrated enrichment of high-yield candidates among BindCraft-designed binders. Our approach enables standardized, large-scale measurement of monomeric yield across diverse proteins, and establishes monomeric yield as a sequence-encoded property that can be learned, predicted and ultimately designed.

title: Colloidal 2D WS2 nanosheets exhibiting high-purity single photon emission
abstract: The search for quantum emitters, delivering single photons "on demand" at cryogenic and elevated temperatures for photonic technologies is ever progressing. For example, micrometer-sized WS2 monolayers exhibit single photon emission by elaborated local defect or strain engineering. Here, we show that wet-chemically synthesised monolayered two-dimensional (2D) WS2 nano sheets (NSs) with lateral sizes of 14 (+/- 6 nm) readily emit single photons from exciton recombination without the need for substrate-induced patterning, strain/defect engineering or spectral filtering. Single particle spectroscopy of 70 individual NSs shows photoluminescence from excitons (2.02 eV), trios (1.94 eV) and defect-localized states (1.85 eV) with fast emission (t1<0.2 ns, t2=3.2 ns), allowing highly frequent excitation cycles. Pulsed at 80 MHz, colloidal WS2 NSs exhibit limited spectral diffusion, no blinking and distinct photon antibunching (g2(0)=0.07 at 5 K), thereby tackling challenges of established colloidal quantum dot systems (blinking, longer emission cycles), while retaining high single photon purity as key quality of deterministic quantum emitters.

title: Neural Stochastic Forecasting for Lateral Molecular Diffusion Simulations
abstract: Predicting the long-time diffusion of membrane proteins is challenging because molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are computationally expensive, while experimental single-particle tracking is often limited by finite observation times. Here, we introduce a neural stochastic (NS) model for forecasting the collective diffusion of membrane proteins from coarse-grained MD trajectories. The model combines a transformer-based representation of protein configurations, recurrent networks operating at multiple temporal scales, and a stochastic latent process with learned memory. A cross-attention decoder then generates correlated protein displacements while accounting for the instantaneous system geometry and periodic boundary conditions. We evaluate the model in two membrane systems: seven interacting PIEZO channels and a mixed system containing seven PIEZO and ten TREK channels. For the seven PIEZO system, the NS model reproduces the anomalous diffusion exponent measured in MD simulations $α\sim 1$, substantially improving on a previously developed variational autoregressive model that exhibits superdiffusive behavior. The model also generates trajectories extending to 40,000 frames and captures the distinct diffusion characteristics of PIEZO and TREK populations in the mixed system. Comparisons of time-averaged mean-square displacements, Van Hove displacement distributions, and non-Gaussian parameters show that the model preserves key statistical features of the simulated dynamics. These results establish neural stochastic modeling as a promising approach for generating long trajectories of multi-protein membrane diffusion and extending the statistical analysis of molecular dynamics simulations.

title: Spin swapping mediated by spin-orbital textures in centrosymmetric multiorbital materials
abstract: Spin swapping converts a primary spin current into a secondary one by interchanging its flow and spin-polarization directions, attributed to spin-orbit scattering or spin-band splitting. Here we uncover a fundamentally distinct route to spin swapping arising from the orbital degree of freedom in the spin pumping to centrosymmetric multiorbital materials \textit{without spin-band splitting}. When the dynamical proximity ferromagnet injects a longitudinal spin current flowing normal to the interface, spin-orbit-entangled orbital textures redirect the injected spins into longitudinal and transverse orbital currents. Their subsequent conversion back to the spin sector generates transverse spin currents with propagation and polarization directions swapped relative to the primary spin current. The swapping efficiency achieves $50\%$ for Ge and Si. Governed by a fourth-rank tensor constrained by crystalline symmetry and without requiring spin-orbit scattering or inversion symmetry breaking, our finding reveals spin-orbital textures as hidden intermediate channels of spin swapping with unexplored material choices and functionalities.

title: Subtle Energy Corrections Reshape Condensed-Phase Property Predictions from a Machine-Learning Interatomic Potential
abstract: Accurate reproduction of electronic-structure labels by machine-learning interatomic potentials does not necessarily ensure reliable condensed-phase properties. We investigate the effects of basis-set superposition error (BSSE) and an explicit Axilrod-Teller-Muto (ATM) three-body dispersion contribution on molecular-liquid predictions. Starting from MACELES-OFF, we fine-tune a baseline potential at the $ω$B97M-V/def2-TZVPD level. A separate branch learns counterpoise (CP) energy and force corrections with the baseline frozen, while a D4-parametrized ATM term is added during molecular-dynamics inference. Mean atom-normalized CP and ATM contributions are 0.222 and 0.205 meV/atom, respectively, for the analyzed SPICE2 configurations from OMol25. We compare baseline, CP-only, ATM-only, and CP + ATM variants for 39 organic liquids. Relative to baseline, the mean system-wise density changes are -1.17%, -10.38%, and -11.93% for CP-only, ATM-only, and CP + ATM, respectively; the corresponding enthalpy-of-vaporization changes are -2.79%, -14.74%, and -18.32%. For the 11 liquids with experimental self-diffusion data, the mean self-diffusion changes are +17.66%, +203.02%, and +230.36%. Both corrections thus lower density and enthalpy of vaporization while increasing molecular mobility on average. ATM dominates these changes, while CP provides a smaller contribution; their combination yields the largest average shifts. These results show that corrections with sub-meV/atom mean values on the analyzed configurations can substantially reshape the predicted structural, thermodynamic, and transport properties of molecular liquids.

title: Ab Initio Accuracy Beyond the Cutoff: Distributed Message-Passing Equivariant Attention at Tens-of-Millions-of-Atom Scale
abstract: Molecular dynamics predicts molecular motion from atomic forces and trajectory integration. Density functional theory (DFT) provides first-principles forces, but its $O(N^3)$ cost limits simulations to thousands of atoms; empirical force fields scale to millions but miss bond breaking and charge transfer. Equivariant message-passing Transformers learn the ab initio potential at linear cost. Stacked layers propagate information beyond a single cutoff, giving four layers a receptive field up to 23Å. At this frontier, scale is limited by communication: layers exchange boundary features across devices, force backpropagation repeats the exchange, and moving atoms change neighbor graphs and tensor shapes. We present Tessera, a distributed runtime that fixes workload shapes between rebuilds. It sorts atoms along a space-filling curve into equal-count shards, ensuring identical atom counts and tensor shapes per rank. Peer sets scale as $K^{0.5}$, not $K$. A conservative neighbor skin preserves topology across updates, enabling each rebuild interval to replay as one CUDA Graph. Fused kernels, three-level neighbor search, and overlapped All-to-All complete it. On 512 GPUs, Tessera sustains 30.7M atoms at 89.7% weak-scaling efficiency (77--90% across three per-GPU loads); per-step time rises 1.11--1.29x as machine and problem grow 16x. Graph reuse cuts full-step time $1.87\times$. Across an $8\times$ device increase, neighbor-search cost grows $1.7\times$, versus $3.0\times$ for Morton order. In a live $10.24$M-atom salt solution, NVE energy drift is $0.42\,μ$eV/atom/ps over $10$ ps, and structure matches a serial reference. A 10.06M-atom Norovirus capsid sustains 100 ps of NVT at $\approx 8$ ps/day on 256 A100 GPUs. Over 200,000 steps, it has no broken bonds or anomalously close pairs and uses three compiled variants, with no graph breaks or eager fallbacks.

title: Where machine learning for enantioselectivity on polysaccharide chiral stationary phases actually fails: a leave-one-paper-out reappraisal of 10,525 enantiomer pairs
abstract: Machine-learning models for enantioselectivity on polysaccharide chiral stationary phases increasingly report high accuracy, but almost always under random data splits. We re-examined this problem on CMRT, the largest public chiral chromatography dataset, curating it into 10,525 enantiomer pairs covering 530 DOI groupsand25columns.Underatrueleave-one-paper-outprotocol,elution-orderaccuracyfallsfrom 66.1 % under a random split to 52.9 %, indistinguishable from a within-paper permutation null (52.3 % ± 0.6).

title: Matrix-dependent transformation governs the chemical identity and biological fate of a metal–organic framework
abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are generally described by their pristine structures, although aqueous use and release expose them to ligands and dissolved ions that can reconstruct their coordination chemistry before biological contact. Here, we follow HKUST-1 across an environmental-to-biological exposure cascade using complementary X-ray methods. Time-resolved Cu K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) and extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy (EXAFS) showed rapid, matrix-specific disruption of the Cu-carboxylate paddlewheel in borehole water (BHW) and…

title: Accept or abstain? A pre-specified test of reliability gates calibrated on held-out chemistry for molecular property and reaction-yield models
abstract: A molecular property or reaction-yield model is useful to a chemist only when it is right on the query in front of them, yet a model’s uncertainty is rarely checked on chemistry it has not seen. We tested an accept-or-abstain protocol in which a gate, scoring each query by its similarity to the training set and by ensemble spread, returns a prediction only when it accepts the query. The gate’s threshold is set by Learn-then-Test to a target precision on a calibration fold held out by chemistry rather than at random.

title: Excited-state dynamics and photo-reaction pathways of 4-nitrothiophenol in solution investigated by time-resolved soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy
abstract: Understanding the molecular pathways underlying light-driven reactions is essential for developing efficient and sustainable photochemical processes. Here, we investigate the photoinduced dynamics and reactivity of deprotonated 4-nitrothiophenol (4-NTP) in aqueous solution using transient nitrogen and oxygen K-edge near-edge X-ray absorption fine structure (NEXAFS) spectroscopy combined with density functional theory (DFT) and equation-of-motion coupled-cluster (EOM-CC) calculations.

title: Aggregation-Driven Self-Inhibition of Grignard Reagents: Insights from DFT and Microkinetic Modeling
abstract: A mechanistic DFT study with explicit Et2O microsolvation and microkinetic modeling unveils how organomagnesium reagents (nBuMgX, X = Cl, Br, nBu) undergo structural reorganization during nitrile additions, generating aggregates that hamper reactivity. Starting from halide-bridged dimers (Et2O)·nBuMg(µ-X)2MgnBu·(Et2O), nitrile addition proceeds via a bimetallic 6-centered transition state (∆G‡ ∼ 19 kcal mol−1) and yields imido-bridged products stabilized by more than 30 kcal mol−1.

title: Schema-guided zero-shot decision models for chemical synthesis argument roles: comparison with supervised ChemBERT
abstract: Jev and Clef outperform a released ChemBERT classifier supervised on the Organic Synthesis Procedures with Argument Roles (OSPAR) corpus on a human-adjudicated Creative Commons (CC) synthesis reference. With supplied mention spans, 17 procedures provide 288 resolved operation–candidate pairs: the positive-role micro-averaged F1 score (the precision–recall harmonic mean) is 96.59% for Jev, 95.27% for Clef and 90.36% for ChemBERT. Fixed role definitions are used without prompt demonstrations or author-performed task-specific fine-tuning; prior OSPAR-based prompt development is disclosed.

title: LANaPDB: A web-based platform for the Latin American Natural Product Database
abstract: Natural products (NPs) have a major impact on several research areas, including drug discovery and development, food and agricultural chemistry, and the cosmetic industry. Annotated compound databases of NPs provide a structured and organized framework that facilitates access to information, particularly if the compound database is freely available. Over the past few years, a compound library from eight countries, called the Latin American Natural Product Database (LANaPDB), has been assembled, curated, and annotated and currently contains 14,741 unique compounds.

title: Electronic Structure Perspective on Cation and Anion Redox in Li2FeS2
abstract: Multielectron redox in Li2FeS2 involves both cation and anion contributions. While prior studies have investigated this process experimentally, questions remain about the Fe-to-S redox transition, persulfide formation, and incomplete delithiation. Here, we revisit the electrochemistry of Li2FeS2 using density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Initial Fe oxidation is shown to proceed via increased Fe−S covalency driven by ligand-to-metal rehybridization. This accounts for only ∼60% of the Fe capacity, after which phase separation into Li1.5FeS2 and Li0.5FeS2 induces a shift to S oxidation.

title: Developing synthetic auxin-based trans-kingdom signaling
abstract: Synthetic trans-kingdom signaling systems with tunable transduction properties provide a unique avenue to explore how communication between organisms coordinate behaviors without the confounding complexity of natural systems. However, existing trans-kingdom signaling systems suffer from either toxic signal molecules, a need for rare precursors for signal generation, or transduction machinery which is either species-specific or cannot be easily tuned. This limits their capacity to be broadly applied across kingdoms and their utility as a model system to study trans-kingdom interactions.

title: Direct NMR evidence for transient binding of the vesicular SNARE protein synaptobrevin-2/VAMP2 to the α-synuclein C-terminus
abstract: The protein -synuclein (-syn) plays a central role in several neurodegenerative diseases, including Parkinson's disease; however, its physiological function remains enigmatic. We provide direct evidence by nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, microscale thermophoresis (MST), and biolayer interferometry (BLI) measurements that the -synuclein C-terminus binds to the vesicular SNARE (soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment protein receptor) protein synaptobrevin-2 (syb-2), also known as VAMP2 (vesicle-associated membrane protein). The observed dissociation constant (Kd) in the 10 - 50 micromolar range falls within the estimated concentration range of -synuclein in neurons, while local concentrations may be substantially higher. NMR chemical shift perturbation (CSP) and paramagnetic relaxation enhancement (PRE) experiments mapped the binding site with residue-specific resolution to the -synuclein C-terminus (V118 - E137) and to the synaptobrevin-2 SNARE motif/linker domain interface (region A82 - K87), and also affected the synaptobrevin-2 N-terminus (M1 - S2). NMR CSPs and PREs indicate a transient interaction in the fast exchange (s-ms) regime. These transient weak binding interactions are characteristic of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) and allow both proteins to engage in multiple binding interactions, thereby enabling -synuclein to play a regulatory role upstream of or during neuronal exocytosis. While the exact physiological role of -synuclein remains debated, the involvement of its pathological form in several neurodegenerative diseases (dubbed synucleinopathies) is well established. Our data suggest a direct link between proteins involved in neurodegeneration and neuronal exocytosis.

title: Paired-probe chemoproteomic strategy enables global site-resolved quantification of lysine redox states
abstract: Site-specific quantification of lysine (Lys) redox states remains unexplored, as current approaches identify only a limited number of modification sites without determining their stoichiometry. Allysine, an oxidized form of Lys, provides a model posttranslational modification (PTM) for addressing this challenge by requiring selective enrichment and site-specific stoichiometric quantification. Here, we developed a quantitative chemoproteomic platform for paired redox-state isotopic stoichiometry mapping of lysine, termed PRISM-Lys. We used an Am-alkyne probe for allysine enrichment by reductive amination and developed a complementary Ald-alkyne probe to label Lys, with identical reactions generating the same chemical product. Coupling this paired-probe strategy with a quantitative chemoproteomic workflow enables global site-resolved quantification and stoichiometric analysis of Lys redox states across cells and tissues. Applied to ferroptosis, PRISM-Lys revealed bidirectional, site-selective remodeling of Lys oxidation events associated with ferroptotic progression. Together, PRISM-Lys establishes a paired-chemistry framework for global, site-resolved quantification of Lys redox states, providing a new quantitative perspective for investigating protein oxidation in biological systems.

title: Evolution of Vesicle Shape Parameters Based on A Deep-Learning Based Image Analysis Framework Over Extended Time Periods
abstract: A precise analysis of shape instabilities in cell-sized membrane compartments requires thorough quantification of the shape dynamics of individual components over extended periods. Herein, we have used phase-contrast microscopy to image giant unilamellar membrane vesicles (GUVs), which are widely used as model systems for cellular structures. GUVs were prepared in the fluid lamellar phase of 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine with and without cholesterol dissolved within a potato starch solution. The morphological changes and budding dynamics of individual GUVs with different chemical compositions were quantified using a deep-learning based image analysis framework over extended time periods, by using phase-contrast micrographs as input data. This automated framework integrates contour-based detection of the mother vesicle with precise segmentation of daughter compartments, thereby enabling explicit identification and tracking of mother and daughter vesicles at high temporal resolution. These findings further facilitate the measurement of the temporal evolution of vesicle morphometrics including area, and local membrane curvature during budding, that can be used as an input to develop computational models aimed at elucidating curvature-driven membrane remodeling in complex soft materials.

title: A Saliva-Inspired Model of Enzymatic Starch Hydrolysis by Alpha Amylase
abstract: We demonstrate that the enzymatic activity of alpha-amylase (AA) can serve as an effective physicochemical trigger for membrane remodeling in giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs). This work provides insight into how primitive protocellular reactions directly translate into the membrane's mechanical responses. Analysis of the potato starch utilized in this work is composed of ~26\% amylose and ~75\% amylopectin. Quantitative DNS analysis revealed time- and concentration-dependent accumulation of reducing sugars during starch degradation by AA. The HPLC-RID chromatograms demonstrated the synthesis of glucose, maltose, maltotriose, maltotetraose, maltopentaose, maltohexaose, and maltoheptaose, with maltose and maltotriose as the major products. The accumulation of these soluble hydrolysis products gradually increases the osmolarity of the extracellular medium surrounding the vesicles, leading to osmotic asymmetry across the membrane. This biochemical framework provides a quantitative basis for understanding membrane deformation, curvature generation, vesicle deflation, and budding. In addition to the specific starch--$\alpha$-amylase system studied here, our work uncovers a general mechanism by which external biochemical reactions control membrane shape transformations via osmotic coupling. Such enzyme-driven remodeling offers a simple yet powerful strategy for inducing dynamic structural changes in artificial cells. It may provide insight into primitive protocellular processes in which metabolic activity and membrane mechanics were inherently coupled.

title: XAMPGen: An Interpretable SI Pipeline For Novel Antimicrobial Peptide Discovery
abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are short peptides with a broad spectrum of activity against bacterial pathogens, representing a promising avenue for combating the growing threat of antibiotic resistance. This study focuses on two main components: 1) generating novel AMPs with desired properties using generative SI (GenSI) and 2) utilizing explainable SI (XSI) methods to validate the GenSI model and derive biological insights. In this work, we fine-tuned ProGen, a decoder-only protein language model, on known AMPs to generate novel peptide sequences with strong antimicrobial properties.

title: CryoID2: deep learning-enhanced identification of protein and RNA from cryoEM maps
abstract: Identifying the molecular components of cryoEM/cryoET maps of endogenous or poorly characterized complexes remains a major bottleneck. CryoID2 addresses this by integrating deep learning-based feature prediction with sequence prioritization and structural evaluation. Three 3D U-Nets extract structure classes, key-atom positions, and reduced residue/nucleotide types from the input map. These predictions support backbone tracing and the generation of short sequence queries that rank candidates from a user-supplied pool-using BLASTp for proteins and a maximin strategy for RNA.

title: Explainable computational framework for subtype classification and biomarker identification in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma using machine learning
abstract: The precise classification of basal, classical, atypical, and mesenchymal subtypes of Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (HNSCC) is crucial for advancing precision oncology. Our research aims to develop an explainable subtype classification model for HNSCC.These molecular subtypes have been previously defined; reliable and meaningful computational methods for the classification of molecular subtypes and prioritization of molecular biomarkers for each subtype do not exist. We developed an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) model that classifies molecular subtypes based on combined transcriptomic profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA-HNSC) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GSE65858). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to quantify the importance of genes for model predictions. Subsequently, genes with high predictive importance were analyzed in protein-protein interactions using STRING, and hub genes were identified by Maximum Clique Centrality (MCC) and used for the identification of candidate biomarkers for each of the subtypes. We employed machine learning methods such as Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), AdaBoost (AB), Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Gaussian Naive Bayes (GNB), XGBoost (XGB), and Gradient Boosting (GB). The XGBoost model achieved an accuracy of 95% after hyperparameter tuning and cross-validation. Biologically relevant subtype-specific biomarkers associated with each molecular subtype were identified. To highlight the potential biological functions of these biomarkers, pathway analysis was performed. Further assessment of these genes, such as survival analysis and druggability, showed promise for the development of targeted therapies.

title: Single-crystal X-ray diffraction of BC8 carbon near terapascal pressures
abstract: Whether carbon forms crystalline structures beyond diamond at terapascal pressures remains unresolved. Predicted for nearly four decades, the denser BC8 phase has lacked direct crystallographic evidence. Here we report the first direct crystallographic identification of BC8 carbon, formed as a single crystal from molten carbon during laser-driven decaying-shock compression of [100]-oriented diamond following loading above 1.1 TPa. Using in situ orientation-resolved single-crystal X-ray diffraction, we observe discrete Bragg spots whose spacings and angular relationships are reproduced by a common orientation matrix within each indexed BC8 reflection group, providing constraints beyond powder peak matching. Our single-crystal formation strategy and direct diffraction evidence resolve the decades-long quest for a post-diamond carbon structure, demonstrating how dynamic loading pathways can make predicted high-pressure phases experimentally accessible.

title: Core Reactivity in Cs-Ba-O ternary system under pressure
abstract: High pressure can activate Cs $5p$ core electrons for covalent bonding. In this study, we investigate the Cs-Ba-O system at 150 and 250 GPa using first-principles structure searches. CsBa$_3$O$_8$ and CsBaO$_4$ both lie on the static-lattice convex hull at 250~GPa and exhibit mild Cs $5p$-O $2p$ bonding while retaining O$_2$ units with intermediate superoxide-peroxide character. Cs$_2$BaO$_3$ shows substantially stronger bonding but remains metastable with respect to CsO and BaO. A 1:1 Cs$_2$O-BaO$_2$ mixture provides a solid starting composition for investigating this chemistry, with core-reactive CsO among the predicted products at 250~GPa. Calculated Cs $L_3$-edge x-ray absorption near-edge spectra and powder diffraction patterns provide electronic and structural signatures to guide identification of the predicted phases in diamond anvil cell experiments.

title: Synchronization transitions in ensembles of active particles with distance-dependent higher-order interactions
abstract: Higher-order interactions are ubiquitous in biological systems and can be used to better describe the ensemble dynamics of self-propelled particles. To this end, this article investigates a Vicsek-Kuramoto model with distance-dependent higher-order interactions and obtains analytical results, albeit under certain assumptions, that characterize its collective dynamics. Subsequently, these are validated through simulations of the system equations, demonstrating both continuous and explosive transitions between the asynchronous and synchronous collective states. Further numerical results also reveal that short-range interactions and tightly clustered initial states can lead to deviations from the theoretical predictions, whereas the latter can be offset by increasing the common self-propulsion velocity. These results offer insights into a broad class of active matter systems with higher-order interactions, and provide a framework for designing and utilizing them for specific applications.

title: Finely tuned DDA-PASEF-based immunopeptidomics workflow enhances HLA class I coverage
abstract: Mass spectrometry-based immunopeptidomics is essential for the direct identification of HLA-presented peptides, but its application to low-input and clinical samples remains challenging. In this study, we present an optimized DDA-PASEF-based workflow to improve HLA class I peptide coverage. First, we optimized a magnetic bead-based sample preparation protocol to support analysis from reduced starting material and increase compatibility with automation. We then evaluated LC gradient length and column dimensions to define complementary configurations for high-throughput and high-coverage analysis. For MS acquisition, we fine-tuned key parameters, including ion accumulation time, number of PASEF scans, ion mobility range, and polygon filtering, to improve sensitivity while maintaining a suitable cycle time and limiting pre-CID truncations. The customized polygon filter improved the detection of singly charged HLA class I peptides, thereby broadening the identified immunopeptide repertoire. Finally, TIMS2Rescore was integrated to improve confidence in peptide identification. Overall, this optimized workflow improves HLA class I immunopeptide coverage across different sample types, even from low injected sample amounts, supporting its future applicability to clinically relevant samples.

title: PANI/CMWCNTs immunosensor with KNN-Ridge for high-throughput COX-2 screening
abstract: Chronic inflammation is tightly linked to atherosclerosis and malignancies. Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) is a pivotal target for anti-inflammatory drug discovery. However, conventional screening approaches for natural products are limited by low throughput, insufficient precision, and prolonged assay durations. Herein, a high-performance COX-2-targeted electrochemical immunosensor was constructed with polyaniline/carboxylated multiwalled carbon nanotube (PANI/CMWCNTs) nanocomposite as conductive sensing interface.

title: Electrostatic control of conformational dynamics drives proton translocation in respiratory Complex I
abstract: Complex I is a large membrane protein that transduces redox energy into a proton motive force across a biological membrane, powering cellular respiration. Yet, despite significant experimental and computational efforts, its long-range proton translocation mechanism remains poorly understood. Here, we combine nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy and site-directed mutagenesis experiments with multiscale classical and hybrid quantum/classical (QM/MM) simulations to probe how conformational dynamics is linked to proton transfer reactions in the terminal antiporter module (Nqo12/NuoL/ND5) of Complex I. We show that protonation of a conserved proton-loading site (Lys329/His241Nqo12) in the terminal antiporter-like module gives rise to conformational changes that result in opening of the proton pathway. We further show that this protonation reaction is controlled by buried ion-pairs that modulate the barrier for proton translocation by intrinsic electric field effects. On a general level, our combined findings reveal how bioenergetic machines combine conformational dynamics with hydration transitions to establish efficient redox-driven proton pumps.

title: A conserved thermodynamic signature links transcriptome organization to growth state
abstract: Living systems operate far from thermodynamic equilibrium, sustaining complexity through continuous free-energy influx and heat dissipation. Yet the higher-order functional constraints imposed by non-equilibrium dynamics remain largely unexplored. To formalize how changes in cellular entropy production constrain intracellular organization across proliferative state transitions, we developed a stochastic-thermodynamic model linking reduced dissipative drive to transient increases in intracellular configurational entropy.

title: Hazard Structure and Repair Kinetics: A 2x2 Classification that Resolves the Stochastic-Death / Individual-Tolerance Dilemma
abstract: The two variants of GUTS (General Unified Threshold model of Survival), stochastic death and individual tolerance, disagree about no-effect concentrations under time-variable exposure, and no standard test separates them. Each variant fixes two independent choices, which form a 2x2 classification: whether the hazard accumulates while damage exceeds a threshold (cumulative) or is set by the highest damage reached (peak-based), and whether repair is proportional or saturating. Calibration fit cannot choose: each structure fits by adjusting its own damage recovery, the cumulative one faster in twelve of fourteen compounds. For two identical pulses separated by complete recovery, the cumulative hazard predicts equal survival through both whatever the parameters, so a carry-over ratio (second-to-first survival) above one excludes it; in Gammarus pulex fourteen of fifteen ratios are at or above one, seven significantly. The peak-based hazard predicts the maximum of the ratio, approached as intervals lengthen in five of six compounds. For organophosphates, whose recovery outlasts the published pulse intervals, the one test on measured damage favours the peak-based hazard: diazinon-exposed Daphnia magna stopped being immobilised once acetylcholinesterase, still inhibited, began to recover. The peak-based hazard is the appropriate default for toxicokinetic-toxicodynamic risk assessment of narcotics and uncouplers, and provisionally of organophosphates.

title: Non-equilibrium cyclic conformations of DNA under electrokinetic confinement
abstract: Classic nanofluidic devices harness geometric confinement to modulate single polymer conformation and control chain dynamics. While classic nanofluidic devices have given rise to a range of applications, they are fundamentally limited by the static nature of their construction, which restricts real time control over molecular conformations. The reversible electrokinetic confinement (RECON) technique enables time-dependent control of DNA conformations in nanowells via dynamic modulation of field-induced confinement. Here, we demonstrate that applying dynamically varying confinement using stochastic and periodic signals can drive the confined polymer to access a range of non-equilibrium states, with the distinct configurations quantified via their radius of gyration tensor. For periodic driving, the device allows controlled cycling across conformational states, with distinct hysteresis observed in the shape anisotropy modulation. We quantify the interplay between the driving frequency, driving amplitude, and resulting hysteresis. Overall, our results establish RECON as a platform for active manipulation of single molecules, opening new avenues for studying non-equilibrium polymer physics and developing high-throughput, dynamically tunable nanofluidic devices.

title: The Test Used to Choose Between Pesticide Survival Models Tracks Lesion Persistence, Not Hazard Structure
abstract: Aquatic pesticide risk assessment predicts survival with toxicokinetic-toxicodynamic models that offer two hazard structures, cumulative or peak-based, which disagree about which exposure patterns are dangerous; for imidacloprid, published choices differ across eight species. The choice is made from one observation: deaths after transfer to clean water are taken to refute the peak-based structure. That inference holds only if damage is falling, which is not measured in these tests but taken from a fitted model. The observation responds to the compound and design, not the hazard structure. Across thirty-two Gammarus pulex treatments the post-exposure death rate places anticholinesterases above uncouplers, in the order of lesion persistence. For diazinon, one series returns opposite verdicts over its sixteen-day window and its first four days. For imidacloprid in Daphnia magna, one damage stage favours the cumulative structure by 78 likelihood units and two stages the peak-based one by 7. Four conditions make a design informative; thirteen of thirty-six treatments in a thirteen-compound archive meet them. Spreading a fixed exposure over longer intervals raises mortality in one of five species, which no repair law reproduces with the kinetics of the models. For neonicotinoids, predictions for such patterns are unvalidated, not conservative.

title: Multispecies transport shapes electrochemical environments in perforated cells
abstract: Cells maintain asymmetric electrochemical environments across selectively permeable plasma membranes. Ion channels on plasma membranes redistribute small ions, whereas large openings such as gasdermin pores allow both ions and proteins to cross the membrane, generating a multispecies transport regime. The transport of charged ions and proteins shapes electrochemical environments, leading to osmolarity changes, which in turn promotes water influx and cell swelling.

title: Learning Constraints in Protein Evolution beyond Known Substitution Frequencies.
abstract: During the evolution of protein sequences, amino acid substitutions follow broad patterns that are well established, such as those induced by the physico-chemical properties of residues or the position of sites along the sequence. While these deviations from random changes have been exploited for practical applications, such as to simulate protein evolution or to score protein alignments, they are too general to predict the precise evolution of individual protein sequences.

title: Isolation of functional endogenous clathrin-coated vesicles and in vitro reconstitution of pure clathrin cages
abstract: Clathrin-coated vesicles (CCVs) mediate key endocytic trafficking events, and dysfunction of CCVs is linked to multiple human diseases. Conventional centrifugation-based purification protocols can enrich endogenous CCVs but fail to eliminate intraluminal smooth vesicles (SVs) and co-isolated exosomes; these lipid contaminants reduce sample homogeneity and hinder high-resolution structural and proteomic analysis. Here, we present an integrated workflow to isolate biologically active endogenous CCVs from porcine brain and reconstitute homogeneous, SV-free clathrin cages. Crude CCVs are first enriched by differential and sucrose density gradient centrifugation to deplete the majority of exosomes. Clathrin cages are then depolymerized under alkaline conditions, allowing separation of soluble clathrin and adaptor proteins from SVs and residual lipid contaminants via ultracentrifugation. Purified coat proteins are reassembled in vitro into uniform clathrin cages. Functional assays confirm that purified CCVs retain Auxilin-Hsc70-dependent uncoating activity, and the enclosed SVs carry active vATPase proton pumps. This approach produces well-defined samples suitable for cryo-electron microscopy and mass spectrometry-based investigation of clathrin assembly and disassembly.

title: Africa gets its first commercial accredited dioxin testing laboratory
abstract: New analytical technique may enable continent to monitor industrial toxic emissions more easily and quickly
authors: Mkhululi Chimoio kaMadala, special to C&EN

title: Complex Martensitic Microstructures in ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$
abstract: We analyze the unusual microstructure resulting from the cubic to orthorhombic phase transformation in the shape-memory alloy ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$. This seems to represent an approximate experimental realization of a deformation having a finite number of incompatible deformation gradients, which has been known to exist only as a theoretical possibility. Because the middle eigenvalue $γ$ of the transformation strain is very close to 1, the phase transformation in this alloy takes place via nucleation of exact austenite-martensite interfaces rather than, as usual for other alloys, by classical austenite-martensite interfaces separating the austenite from a finely-twinned laminate of martensite. According to the moving mask approximation of Della Porta this leads to the question whether a microstructure can be formed from the set $H$ of the twelve matrices ${\mathbf V}_i$ on the martensite energy wells that are rank-one connected to the identity, even though these matrices are mutually incompatible. We show that when $γ=1$ and the transformation is volume preserving, such a microstructure is possible that does not deform the grain boundary. This is a consequence of $H$ forming a degenerate $T_{12}$ configuration in the sense of Kirchheim. In fact there are such microstructures supported on just 8 of the 12 matrices in $H$. However there is no deformation satisfying the same boundary condition whose gradient belongs to $H$ almost everywhere. An additional prediction, confirmed experimentally, is that the macroscopic deformation gradient equals the identity everywhere. We also analyse the approximate compatibility of the ${\mathbf V}_i$. Although mutually incompatible, they are nearly compatible, with some pairs much more nearly compatible than others, these pairs corresponding to interfaces that are more frequently observed.

title: KolTa: A Physics-Informed Active Learning Framework for Formulation Discovery with Limited Data
abstract: Finding high-performing formulations is difficult when few have been measured and experimental budgets are limited. We propose KolTa, an active learning framework that selects batches to discover the top 5% of formulations at a target temperature under a fixed query budget. KolTa combines a three-stage predictor of component contributions, role-conditioned interactions, and anchored temperature response with task-specific soft physics constraints. Its Physics-Residual-Calibrated Upper Confidence Bound (PRC-UCB) acquisition rule combines predicted utility, ensemble disagreement, and a target-temperature physics residual, with nonnegative exploration weights fitted to out-of-fold signed errors. We evaluate the framework on three measured tasks and one simulated task covering binary-mixture viscosity, drug solubility, ionic-liquid viscosity, and electrolyte conductivity. KolTa ranks first or second in mean area under the learning curve (AULC) on every task and outperforms seven of the eight comparator strategies in paired tests, winning 75 of 78 paired comparisons across tasks and seeds against those seven strategies. Across the three measured tasks, its largest gap to the best mean AULC is 0.032, compared with at least 0.056 for every comparator. On Drug, reaching 80% average recovery of the remaining targets across drugs requires an estimated median of 348 additional formulation queries, about 18% fewer than the fastest comparator. Researchers can adapt the framework to diverse formulation problems through component roles and physical constraints.

title: Strain control of magneto-optical properties of ultra-thin Ni-Mn-Ga films grown by magnetron sputtering
abstract: Ultra-thin epitaxial Ni-Mn-Ga films, 10-15 nm thick, were grown by magnetron sputtering on MgO(001), either directly on the substrate or on a Cr buffer, and studied by X-ray diffraction, magnetometry, and magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) spectroscopy. The films were austenitic, with the cubic cell tetragonally distorted in opposite directions. The film on bare MgO was stretched in-plane ($c/a=0.989$) and the film on Cr was compressed in-plane ($c/a=1.021$), while their unit-cell volumes differed by less than $0.3\%$. As the thermal expansion mismatch was expected to stretch the films in-plane in both cases, the opposite distortions were attributed to the lattice misfit. The room-temperature magnetization loops of the two films did not show significant differences, but their polar and longitudinal MOKE spectra differed in the amplitude, sign, and energy of the spectral structures over the whole 0.76-5 eV range. Magneto-optical simulations showed that the absence of the Cr buffer accounted only for the stronger low-energy polar MOKE rotation extremum of the film on MgO. We attributed the other changes to the strain-induced change of the electronic structure, consistent with theoretical predictions in which the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ sub-bands of the minority-spin Ni $e_g$ states exchange their order when the distortion changes sign. In parts of the spectrum, the two films showed Kerr rotation or ellipticity of opposite sign, so the choice of the growth template or a dynamically induced distortion can switch the sign of the magneto-optical response at a given photon energy.

title: Discrete Backbone Elasticity and Curvature-Dependent Torsion Statistics in Proteins
abstract: Coarse-grained models of protein conformational dynamics use $\mathrm{C}_α$ geometry to describe the probabilities of regular helices, ordered turns and disordered conformations. To test how much of this order arises from local chain elasticity, we connect discrete Hasimoto frame transport to neighboring bending mismatch, deriving a curvature-product torsion interaction and a six-parameter generalized von Mises density. Fitted on 194 chains from the ATLAS molecular dynamics database and tested on 1744 sequence-nonredundant proteins, this baseline reduces negative log-density loss from 1.490 to 1.160 nats, torsion-sign error from 12.26 to 2.15 percentage points, and helix-fraction error from 21.84 to 10.41 points. Ablations and circular-moment projections against reference generative models motivate extensions to anisotropic stiffness and two partition-function-weighted elastic states, further lowering test loss to 0.790 nats and helix error to 1.65 points. The fixed hierarchy also improves predictions across 72 trajectories of peptides $\mathrm{Fs}$ and $(\mathrm{AAQAA})_3$ and miniprotein $\mathrm{HP35}$ spanning varied starting conformations and force fields. Remaining angular errors in these trajectories are associated with atomic context at shared bends, as bend-matched peptide frames adopt opposite torsion signs with distinct hydrogen-bond patterns and a proline-containing $\mathrm{HP35}$ turn remains at negative torsion. Introducing a bilinearly coupled $\mathrm{C}_α$--$\mathrm{N}$ orientation angle largely reparameterizes the existing bend-dependent harmonics, with an empirical $L^2$ Gram projection placing 96.7\% to 99.6\% of its added coefficient-function squared norm within the original six-function span. These results link discrete Hasimoto elasticity to statistical backbone potentials and clarify the scope and limits of local $\mathrm{C}_α$ geometry.

title: Digital health technologies and measurable management outcomes in primary care: A systematic review, descriptive quantitative synthesis, and temporal sensitivity analysis
abstract: The rapid digital transformation of primary health care has integrated electronic health records (EHRs), telemedicine, mobile health (mHealth), artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and natural language processing (NLP) into routine service management. However, evidence on their relationship with operational efficiency and management performance remains fragmented. This systematic review synthesized evidence on digital health technologies and measurable management outcomes in primary care, including waiting times, administrative efficiency, resource utilization, operating costs, and patient or professional satisfaction. Following PRISMA 2020 principles and the PICO framework, searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, and IEEE Xplore for records published from January 1, 2018, to October 7, 2025. A structured eligibility audit reduced the candidate analytical corpus from 256 records to 172 studies included in the final descriptive quantitative synthesis. Telemedicine/mHealth was the largest category (n = 98; 57.0%), followed by EHR/interoperability (n = 35; 20.3%) and AI/ML or predictive analytics (n = 29; 16.9%). The most frequent indicators were patient or professional satisfaction (n = 24) and operating costs (n = 20). Because of methodological heterogeneity, formal meta-analysis was not performed. Temporal sensitivity analysis showed continuity in EHR/interoperability and telemedicine/mHealth, with a recent increase in AI/ML representation. A stratified preliminary JBI check in 40 studies found mostly low or moderate risk classifications, but it was used only to contextualize reporting quality and does not represent a full risk-of-bias assessment of all 172 studies.

title: STEK: Structural-Terrain-Enhanced Koopman-Inspired Cross-Channel Regularization for Retrospective Battery Multi-Target Estimation
abstract: Retrospective battery characterization across heterogeneous cells is challenging because cycling records vary substantially with chemistry, protocol, cell format, capacity, and operating conditions. An endpoint charge--discharge curve captures the local condition of an evaluated cycle, while a cell-level lifecycle terrain summarizes structural evolution across the archived trajectory. We propose STEK, a structural-terrain-enhanced framework for retrospective battery multi-target estimation. STEK combines a cell-level lifecycle (dQ/dV) terrain with an endpoint-derived structural proxy through quality-proxy-conditioned gating. Bounded FiLM and a validity-gated residual head refine the endpoint-curve representation while preserving a curve-based prediction pathway. Battery-type and optional material-text representations further condition an identity-centered low-rank linear map, providing a Koopman-inspired cross-channel consistency objective without modeling temporal dynamics or performing rollout. Under the fixed seven-output MIX-battery protocol, the full retrospective setting improves aggregate performance over endpoint-only learned baselines across multiple temporal backbones; this comparison reflects both the additional archived context and the modeling design. Under matched auxiliary inputs, STEK outperforms direct concatenation and quality-unaware FiLM, while descriptor-removal tests show graceful fallback to the endpoint pathway. Deterministic rules remain preferable for directly recoverable capacity summaries. The method targets retrospective archive harmonization rather than online estimation from cycle t alone.

title: All reweighted paths lead to Rome: Unification of reweighting schemes for stratified path sampling
abstract: Path sampling-based stratification algorithms such as Transition Interface Sampling (TIS) enable the evaluation of kinetic rate constants and mechanisms of complex molecular rare event transitions. By sampling only short dynamical trajectories, TIS allows constructing an estimate of the unbiased dynamics by reweighting the interface path ensembles. In the past decades several methods have been developed and applied to achieve such path reweighting, based on statistically optimal use of the trajectory data. Why and how this reweighting exactly works has been underexplored up to now. Here we discuss several different schemes to compute the reweighted path ensemble (RPE), notably point-wise matching, Weighted Histogram Analysis Method (WHAM), Multistate Bennett Acceptance Ratio (MBAR), variance based reweighting (VBR) and survival analysis reweighting (SAR). We show that except for the point-wise matching the other methods are leading to the same outcome, and in fact can be seen as identical. Moreover, the SAR links to a well-established nonparametric maximum-likelihood estimator of product-limit form. This allows a synthesis of all path reweighting schemes, identifying the common underlying nature. All schemes follow from this common origin. We illustrate the reweighting with some simple examples, and show that care has to be taken when applying WHAM, if the number of interfaces and histogram bins do not match.

title: Learning Noise Optimization for Reward Alignment in Few-Step Generative Models
abstract: Reward alignment for diffusion- and flow-based generative models is often formulated over stochastic trajectories, making it less suitable for few-step deterministic generators. Initial noise optimization provides a trajectory-free alternative, but existing gradient-free methods require costly per-sample search at inference. We introduce LeNO (Learning Noise Optimization), which amortizes reward-guided initial noise optimization into a learned residual transport while keeping the pretrained generator frozen. LeNO learns an anchor-conditioned distribution over noise corrections using Local GRPO and scalar rewards, eliminating iterative test-time optimization. For Gaussian initial noise with norm-preserving projection, we derive a tractable upper bound on the KL divergence between the corrected noise distribution and the original prior, providing a principled regularization objective. We evaluate LeNO on few-step text-to-image and protein structure generation, including expensive black-box designability rewards. Across both domains, LeNO improves target rewards with a single noise correction at inference while largely preserving generation quality and diversity.

title: An All-Atom Model of the Resorcinol-Formaldehyde Aerogel Skeleton from DFT and Molecular Dynamics: Validation and Iron Incorporation
abstract: Resorcinol-formaldehyde (RF) aerogels are lightweight, ultra-porous thermal superinsulators whose complex amorphous structure has not yet been described at the all-atom level. Here, we build an all-atom model of the RF aerogel skeleton by combining density functional theory (DFT) and classical molecular dynamics (MD), validate it against experimental infrared and density measurements, and use it to study the incorporation of iron dopants. The RF base unit was optimized with Gaussian, DMol$^{3}$ and SIESTA, and its calculated infrared spectrum agreed with experiment. Comparing classical force fields with DFT for branched systems of two to four base units (140-278 atoms) led to the choice of COMPASS II. A 15,012-atom system of 54 branched RF units, not cross-linked to each other, aggregated into a single cluster in the canonical (NVT) ensemble and reached an equilibrium density of 1.296 g.cm$^{-3}$ in the isobaric-isothermal (NPT) ensemble, in agreement with the experimental skeletal density (1.3 g.cm$^{-3}$). Then, 5 wt$\%$ iron (109 atoms) was added to the equilibrated structure: during 1 ns of NPT simulation, the fraction of iron atoms embedded in the skeleton rose from 63$\%$ to 71$\%$, and the Fe-C radial distribution function peaked at 3 Å. The model thus provides an experimentally supported starting point for screening fillers and dopants in RF gels, with prospective application to their thermoelectric functionalization, which we have previously demonstrated experimentally with basalt and PANOX fibres. Future extensions could address skeleton properties relevant to thermal insulation and the pyrolysis of RF gels into carbon and metal-doped carbon aerogels.

title: Quantitatively Probing the Tilt Angle Failures in 4D-STEM Polarisation Analysis
abstract: Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) is increasingly used to map polarisation in ferroic textures such as domain walls, vortices, merons and skyrmions. These textures are accompanied by local strain, lattice rotation and misorientation, which also modulate the diffraction features used to infer polar order. Even small deviations from the zone axis can therefore produce contrast that is indistinguishable from a polarisation signal. Here we quantify the tilt sensitivity of two polarisation-sensitive signals, diffraction disc intensity and Kikuchi band intensity, in three ferroelectrics with distinct polar distortions: PbTiO3, BaTiO3 and Cu3B7O13Cl boracite. We find that tilts of only 0.01-0.05 degrees reverse most Friedel-pair disc asymmetries, and even the most robust disc pairs reverse by 0.04 degrees in BaTiO3, 0.14 degrees in PbTiO3 and 0.18 degrees in boracite, producing contrast equal and opposite to that of the polarisation.
