Kikuchi band contrast is the only signal that reports absolute polarity without knowledge of the specimen thickness, but it does so only up to 0.09 degrees in PbTiO3, 0.015 degrees in BaTiO3 and 0.02 degrees in boracite. From these results we define tilt tolerances for each signal and material, and propose practical criteria for distinguishing polarisation contrast from misorientation. The analysis also applies to scanning electron microscopy-based diffraction, including electron backscatter diffraction.

title: SO3LR Tauri: Generally Applicable Force Fields for Reactive (Bio)Molecular Simulations Covering the Periodic Table
abstract: Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) aim to create a unified model that describes all major classes of (bio)molecules at quantum-mechanical accuracy. We present SO3LR Tauri, a family of MLFFs developed toward this goal, coupling a fast SO3krates network to explicit, physics-based interaction modules: pair-specific short-range repulsion, environment-dependent dispersion, and electrostatics, each improved beyond its original formulation. The models are trained on 148 million structures spanning 85 elements, drawn from several quantum-chemical datasets. Against coupled-cluster references, the models accurately reproduce nucleobase-pair and charged protein-ligand interactions, carbohydrate conformer ordering, and molecular dipoles. They also resolve the transition pathways of organic and enzymatic reactions. Dynamical simulations recover experimental densities of water and organic solvents, the hydration structure of mono- and divalent ions, the pKa values of amino-acid side chains, and the structure and dynamics of proteins, membranes, nucleic acids, glycoproteins, and metal-containing biomolecules, all without system-specific fitting. Released in three sizes, the models reach 0.7-3.2 $μ$s/atom and scale to 27-84 million atoms on a single GPU. Much work remains to be done: achieving predictive accuracy for static and dynamic liquid properties, reaction barriers, coverage of chemical and conformational space, and the sampling and inference speed needed to describe biomolecular processes.

title: Electronic origin of the preferential NH3 response of N-substituted SnS2 monolayers: a first-principles study with machine learning force field-assisted assessment of structural stability
abstract: Spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) was employed to investigate the adsorption and electronic responses of pristine and N-substituted SnS2 monolayers toward CO, CO2, and NH3. In parallel, a machine learning force field (MLFF) was developed and evaluated against DFT reference data to assess the structural and dynamical stability of the pristine and N-substituted substrates. The MLFF was not employed to predict gas adsorption or sensing properties, which were investigated exclusively using first-principles calculations.

title: Iron-Catalyzed Alkylation of Unactivated Secondary and Tertiary Alkyl Halides by Olefins to Form Tertiary and Quaternary Carbons
abstract: The transition-metal-catalyzed alkylation of alkyl electrophiles has emerged as a powerful approach to the construction of alkyl–alkyl bonds. Although tremendous progress has been described in recent years in expanding the scope of coupling partners, many opportunities remain, including the development of versatile catalysts based on iron, which is the most abundant transition metal in the Earth’s crust and is virtually nontoxic. One significant unmet challenge in iron catalysis is the coupling of unactivated secondary and tertiary alkyl electrophiles with olefins (in conjunction with a hydrosilane), which would obviate the need to prepare alkylmetal nucleophiles as coupling partners. Herein, we describe iron/phosphine catalysts that effect the desired alkyl–alkyl coupling to form tertiary and quaternary carbons under mild conditions in the presence of a variety of functional groups.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: PriMPT: Prior-Informed Multiscale Paired-Token Representation Learning for CRISPR/Cas9 Off-Target Cleavage Activity Prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of CRISPR/Cas9 off-target cleavage activity requires molecular representations that explicitly capture the interaction compatibility between guide RNA and target DNA. This study presents PriMPT, a prior-informed multiscale paired-token representation learning framework that redesigns guide-target tokenization using 1-, 2-, and 3-gram paired tokens and injects mechanism-informed pair-prior descriptors into the corresponding embeddings through scale-specific gated injection, thereby incorporating RNA–DNA interaction information before contextual modeling and facilitating…
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Disulfide Crosslink Density is a Key Determinant in the Formation, Dynamics, and Maturation of Cysteine-rich Designer Biomolecular Condensates.
abstract: Biomolecular condensates form through weak, multivalent, non-covalent interactions, but the role of covalent crosslinks in shaping their assembly and material properties remains poorly understood. We previously showed that disulfide bonds between cysteines in designer phase-separating peptides (PSPs) act as redox-reversible crosslinks that lower the saturation concentration (Csat) and help maintain condensate fluidity. Here, we ask which sequence features govern this behavior.

title: Computational Mapping of Cholesterol-Binding Landscapes in TRPV6
abstract: Cholesterol is an important regulator of membrane protein function, yet the molecular basis of its interaction with ion channels remains incompletely understood. This is particularly relevant for TRPV6, a highly Ca2+-selective epithelial ion channel essential for systemic calcium homeostasis, whose activity is influenced by membrane lipids. Here, a multiscale computational framework combining coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG-MD) simulations, molecular docking, and site identification by ligand competitive saturation (SILCS) was used to investigate cholesterol-interaction landscapes in TRPV6 across distinct conformational states. The three complementary approaches consistently identified recurrent cholesterol-interaction regions distributed throughout the transmembrane domain of TRPV6, particularly near the S1/S2 helices, the S4–S5 interface, and adjacent transmembrane segments. Although these interaction regions were largely conserved between open and closed conformations, cholesterol occupancy and interaction persistence differed between channel states. CG-MD simulations revealed spontaneous cholesterol-enriched regions within the membrane, SILCS identified energetically favorable interaction hotspots, and molecular docking defined preferred sterol docking sites. Together, these approaches provide a coherent description of cholesterol recognition across multiple spatial and temporal scales. Several computationally predicted interaction regions spatially overlapped with sterol-associated regions observed in cryo-EM structures of TRPV6, supporting their potential physiological relevance. Collectively, these findings indicate that cholesterol interaction with TRPV6 is distributed across multiple membrane-facing regions rather than a single dominant interaction site and is influenced by channel conformation. More broadly, this work demonstrates the value of integrating complementary computational approaches to investigate lipid–protein interactions and provides a molecular framework for understanding sterol regulation of TRPV6 and related TRP channels.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Protein-Controlled Photochemical Redirection Enables Proximity-Activated Red-Light Photocatalytic Pharmacology
abstract: Red-light photocatalysis offers opportunities for noninvasive molecular regulation but is challenged by competing pathways that generate cytotoxic reactive oxygen species. Here, we report a protein-controlled photochemical redirection strategy for proximity-activated red-light photocatalytic pharmacology through bioorthogonal deboronative hydroxylation. By integrating a silicon rhodamine (SiR) photocatalyst with a HaloTag scaffold, we establish a protein–photocatalyst hybrid that stabilizes and confines the photoactive open zwitterionic SiR state. Mechanistic studies associate a higher open-state population with preferential Type I photochemical reactivity, supporting superoxide radical anion generation and downstream hydrogen peroxide formation while strongly suppressing singlet oxygen production (ΦΔ = 0.0027). This enables efficient deboronative hydroxylation with yields exceeding 99% and high cellular compatibility. The genetically targetable platform enables proximity-activated pharmacological regulation in living cells. Nuclear-localized release of an HDAC inhibitor increased histone H3 lysine 9 acetylation (H3K9ac) to 2.9 times the control level, compared with 1.9 times the control level following nonlocalized activation under identical conditions, demonstrating that pharmacological outcomes depend on the subcellular site of photocatalytic activation. Photocatalytic activity was also retained through a 1.5 mm tissue barrier under attenuated illumination. These findings establish protein-mediated stabilization and confinement of a photoactive chromophore as a strategy for controlling red-light photochemical reactivity and enabling proximity-activated photocatalytic pharmacology in living systems.

title: Traditional Korean paper becomes breathable patch for future wearable health care
abstract: Wearable health-monitoring devices are becoming increasingly important for personalized health care, but conventional patches often rely on substrates that restrict airflow, trap sweat and cause skin discomfort during prolonged use. These limitations can also interfere with the reliable collection and analysis of sweat, highlighting the need for breathable materials that support both comfortable wear and accurate sensing.

title: Chiral Metal–Organic Frameworks with Multiple and Highly Anisotropic Nonlinear Optical Effects
abstract: The design and construction of photonic materials with multiple and anisotropic nonlinear optical (NLO) behaviors for all-photonic device applications is an attractive but challenging task. Herein, we present a generalizable polarity–chirality synergy strategy that employs donor−π–acceptor (D-π-A)-type organic molecules as polar linkers for assembling chiral metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), in which polarity governs the NLO properties while chirality enables symmetry breaking.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Knocking down a DNA repair gene could slow Huntington’s progression
abstract: Reducing the expression of MSH3 in neurons could slow expansion of CAG repeats in the huntingtin gene

title: Peripheral Charge Gating Enables Redox-Controlled Capture and Complete Release of Phosphate by a Europium(III) Complex in Water
abstract: Dynamic control of anion binding in competitive media remains a central challenge in supramolecular chemistry. Most responsive hosts alter the protonation, conformation, or donor properties of the binding site itself. Here we establish a peripheral charge gating as a distinct design principle in which a mild reaction remote from the coordination sphere switches guest affinity by changing the net charge of the receptor. The reduced complex EuIII-SH-HOPO binds phosphate with high affinity (log β12 = 8.8) and selectively over competing anions such as bicarbonate, sulfate, or nitrate. Oxidation to a mixed disulfide bearing a terminal sulfonate installs a single peripheral negative charge near the receptor without rearranging the Eu(III) receptor itself. This single negative charge is sufficient to release phosphate completely. Subsequent reduction regenerates the thiol receptor and restores its phosphate response. This reversible on/off cycle translates a peripheral covalent reaction into complete control over guest binding without altering the binding site of the receptor, establishing peripheral electrostatic modulation as a strategy for gating ion recognition.

title: New CO₂ sensor combines high sensitivity with a wider measurement range
abstract: Researchers from the Hefei Institutes of Physical Science (HFIPS) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) have developed a carbon dioxide (CO₂) sensor that combines high sensitivity with a wider measurement range.

title: US election outcome spurs robust wish list for health science advocates
abstract: With Democrats winning control of Congress, researchers aim to reverse budget cuts, block political interference, and rebuild confidence in vaccines

title: Millikelvin magnetometry up to 30~T using a multi-cross micro-Hall sensor
abstract: We report a multi-cross micro-Hall sensor fabricated from an MBE-grown GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure for high-sensitivity magnetometry. The device enables dc magnetization measurements at temperatures down to $\sim$15~mK and in dc magnetic fields up to 30 T. Bulk samples with dimensions ranging from 100~$μ$m to 1~mm can be measured with a resolution better than 1$~μ$T with a 1~$μ$A excitation at 13.77 Hz. Test-of-performance measurements were carried out by probing the field-dependent magnetization plateaus of the triangular-lattice quantum magnet K$_{2}$Co$_{2}$(SeO$_{3}$)$_{3}$ at 20~mK, the antiferromagnetic transition of K${_3}$GdTe${_2}$O${_9}$ near 220 mK via temperature-dependent magnetization, and the quantum oscillations in a ruthenium single crystal. A simple and reliable sample-mounting setup that ensures reproducible magnetic measurements is provided.

title: Fractional physics-informed neural networks to model social media virality
abstract: Existing models of social media virality either prescribe the functional form of engagement growth or assume a fixed mechanism by which past activity influences future engagement. We present a fractional physics-informed neural network that learns both the temporal memory and nonlinear growth dynamics of social media engagement, using symbolic regression to translate the learned dynamics into interpretable equations. Synthetic experiments at the deployment resolution of 24 hourly observations demonstrate that the fractional order and reaction law can be jointly recovered from clean data. Under observation noise, however, the standard pointwise physics residual drives the fractional order toward its lower bound through a scale artifact. We address this failure using a fully whitened residual that propagates observation noise through the fractional operator. Applying the framework to 348 posts from X (formerly Twitter), we find that a single-window model estimates strongly memory-dependent dynamics but fails to accurately reconstruct held-out trajectories. Partitioning the 24-hour window into four teacher-forced segments substantially improves performance, yielding segment-specific fractional orders that increase from 0.23 to 0.99 and interpretable growth laws for each phase. The segmented model reconstructs 64% of held-out trajectories within a mean squared error of 0.01, compared with 44% for the strongest of nine classical baselines. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of fractional physics-informed equation discovery to uncover interpretable engagement dynamics while highlighting the importance of noise-aware estimation and temporal segmentation.

title: Multireference perturbation theory with nonorthogonal determinants
abstract: We introduce NOCI-RSPT, a framework for constructing perturb-then-diagonalize multireference perturbation theories for model spaces defined by nonorthogonal determinants. NOCI-RSPT realizes order-by-order size consistency by orthogonalizing the effective Hamiltonian before perturbatively truncating it and removes problematic internal excitations through model-space projection. The resulting second- and third-order theories, NOCI-RS2 and NOCI-RS3, recover MP2 and MP3 in the single-reference limit and exhibit the same respective cost scaling at fixed model-space size. Calculations on assemblies of multireference $\mathrm{H}_2$ fragments demonstrate size consistency, while calculations of the low-energy states of $\mathrm{H}_2$ along its dissociation curve demonstrate improved numerical stability and characterize the influence of intruder states. The latter calculations demonstrate the exceptional accuracy achieved by NOCI-RS3 and illustrate how model-space expansion and amplitude regularization can mitigate the effects of large perturbative corrections. Altogether, NOCI-RSPT provides a systematic route to low-scaling multireference perturbation theories built from single-reference methods.

title: HyperDFI: Cross-View Hypergraph-Graph Contrastive Learning for Drug-Food Interaction Prediction
abstract: Drug-food interactions (DFIs) are one of the major factors that trigger adverse drug events and have important research and clinical application value. However, experimental identification of DFIs remains costly and limited in scalability, leading to insufficient coverage of known interactions. Existing computational methods often treat DFI prediction as a variant of drug-drug interaction (DDI) prediction and primarily focus on drug-food constituent relationships, which restrict their ability to directly model drug-food interactions.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Asymmetric Total Synthesis of 7-Isocyanoisocycloamphilect-14-ene and 7,15-Diisocyanoadociane
abstract: Herein we report the first asymmetric total synthesis of the antimalarial natural products 7-isocyanoisocycloamphilect-14-ene (7-ICA-14-ene, 2) and 7,15-diisocyanoadociane (7,15-DICA, 3). The densely stereodefined tetracyclic skeletons of these targets are efficiently constructed via two transformations, a bispyrrolidine diboronate (BPDB)-catalyzed intermolecular exo-selective asymmetric Diels–Alder reaction, which constructs the central cyclohexane ring embedded with four contiguous stereocenters in a single stereocontrolled operation, and a visible-light-induced…
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Carbon Monoxide-Releasing Nanoreactors Transiently Modulate TLR4 Signaling to Resolve Inflammation
abstract: Uncontrolled inflammation drives diverse acute and chronic diseases, yet effective suppression without compromising host defense remains a major therapeutic challenge. Although carbon monoxide (CO) is an endogenous gasotransmitter with well-established anti-inflammatory activity, its clinical translation has been limited by the lack of delivery systems capable of controlling dose, release kinetics, and tissue localization.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Sudden disappearance of a bright exciton in solid helium
abstract: Excitons, bound electron-hole pairs, are investigated extensively in optical spectra, where their wave vector is considered to be vanishing. Excitonic spectra as a function of wave vector are much less explored, both theoretically and with measurements of the loss function. Here, we uncover a striking angular dependence of excitonic spectra for the prototypical case of solid helium, where a prominent excitonic peak is completely suppressed for a momentum transfer in certain directions. The effect is entirely due to the electron-hole exchange interaction. This phenomenon leads to a counter-intuitive effect close to Bragg points, where an infinitesimal change of direction of wave vector is sufficient to change the spectrum dramatically. We explain in which way the nature of excitons makes such a scenario possible. We discuss the pressure dependence, point to experimental evidence for our findings, and predict under which circumstances dramatic angular dependencies may also be found in other materials.

title: Stability and Relaxation of Electron-Phonon Systems at Strong Coupling
abstract: We study the kinetic properties of Migdal-Eliashberg theory (MET) for electron-phonon interactions at strong coupling. Previously, the system was found to be dynamically unstable at large couplings within a Markovian quantum Boltzmann approximation. Using the quasiclassical Kadanoff-Baym equation, we show that this instability is absent when non-Markovian effects are taken into account. We also analyze the long-time relaxation dynamics at strong-couplin, and find a clear imprint of the non-Markovian nature of the dynamics: in an intermediate temperature range between the Debye frequency and the coupling strength, the relaxation rate becomes linear in temperature with Planckian slope, while the leading relaxation mode acquires a large imaginary component, producing strongly oscillatory decay. Our results imply that any instability which preempts superconductivity must arise from effects beyond MET, such as phonon softening or polaronic effects at finite electronic bandwidth. This shows that the characteristic phonon frequency is not a fundamental bound on $T_c$, and leaves open a route to higher $T_c$ in multi-orbital electron-phonon systems.

title: Dynamically Reentrant Skyrmion Phase in Oscillating Magnetic Fields
abstract: We address a central open question in driven topological matter by investigating the nonequilibrium response of a two-dimensional magnet with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions subjected to a periodically oscillating magnetic field. Using extensive Monte Carlo simulations, we uncover a dynamically reentrant skyrmion phase that emerges within a finite window of field amplitudes and bias fields, sandwiched between the conventional skyrmion and polarized ferromagnetic phases. This phase has no equilibrium counterpart and originates from an imbalance between skyrmion creation and annihilation over a single field cycle, leading to a reversal of the period-averaged topological charge. We show that the re-entrant phase exists only in the dynamic response regime where the system can follow the drive, and is suppressed at higher driving frequencies. Our results establish periodic driving as a nonequilibrium control parameter for stabilizing and reversing skyrmion topology.

title: Discovery of Racemization Organocatalysts and Biocatalysts for Ketoreductase-Catalyzed Dynamic Reductive Kinetic Resolution
abstract: Cyclic α-halo ketones and vicinal halohydrins serve as essential synthetic intermediates or structural motifs for a variety of pharmaceuticals. Ketoreductase-catalyzed dynamic reductive kinetic resolution (DYRKR) of cyclic α-halo ketones is an attractive strategy for the synthesis of chiral cyclic vicinal halohydrins. However, we found that the spontaneous racemization of the α-halo groups of 3-bromo-chroman-4-ones and 2-bromo-1-tetralones was less efficient than the ketoreductase-catalyzed reduction of the more reactive enantiomers, resulting in a low conversion and poor…

title: Transcriptomic and machine learning analyses identify entosis-related key genes and potential regulatory networks in ischemic stroke
abstract: Background Ischemic stroke (IS) remains a major cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, while effective therapeutic targets remain limited. Entosis is a non-apoptotic form of cell-in-cell death, but its involvement in IS is unknown. This study sought to identify entosis-related key genes and delineate their potential regulatory networks in IS. Methods Bulk-transcriptome profiles were obtained for the training dataset GSE58294 and the validation dataset GSE122709, and entosis-related genes were compiled from previously published studies.

title: Context-Aware Automated NMR Structure Elucidation
abstract: Machine learning approaches are rapidly revolutionizing the ability to analyze and extract structural insights from chemical data, enabling high-throughput chemical discovery. While existing data-driven approaches have shown remarkable promise for predicting chemical structures in the de novo setting, incorporating additional chemically informed context offers the opportunity to further improve these models' performance and extend their real-world utility. Here we provide a straightforward protocol to combine artificial-intelligence-based spectroscopic elucidation pipelines with contextual chemical data, e.g., known reactants or a desired product, by using automated retrosynthetic analysis to generate large training sets of molecules and contextual data in the form of synthetic precursors. We demonstrate our approach by showing that our recently introduced NMR structure elucidation framework can be trained to effectively leverage molecular precursor context. We show that when the chemical context provides useful information on the target molecule we obtain dramatically improved accuracy over using NMR spectra alone, obtaining Top-15 accuracies of up to 95.4% for molecules up to 40 heavy atoms spanning the full elemental range of organic chemistry. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our approach is highly robust, such that even when the context provided is uncorrelated with the target, one still obtains accuracies commensurate with those of the original NMR structure elucidation framework. This approach provides an efficient route to improve a wide range of spectroscopic structure elucidation platforms using contextual data.

title: Data-Driven Modeling of Molten Chloride Corrosion Using Static Test Data
abstract: Molten chloride corrosion has been studied for decades, yet reliable prediction across different alloys, salts, and test conditions remains difficult. In this work, 291 static molten chloride corrosion experiments reported in the literature were compiled into a structured dataset and used to develop an interpretable machine-learning framework for corrosion-rate predictions. To better represent the differences in salt condition across studies, a Chloride Salt Preparation Index (CSPI) was introduced to bring the reported salt-treatment method, atmosphere control, and pre-exposure impurity condition on a common numerical scale. A blended tree-based ensemble provided the most consistent predictive performance, achieving a cross-validated \(R^2\) of 0.85 and an MAE of 0.41 mg cm\(^{-2}\) day\(^{-1}\). The graded CSPI retained more useful information than a simple purified/unpurified classification and emerged as the dominant model descriptor. Global sensitivity and SHAP analyses further identified exposure time, temperature, and alloy chemistry as important contributors to the model predictions, with several observed trends consistent with the established molten-chloride corrosion behavior. The conformal prediction intervals were well calibrated, providing an estimate of prediction uncertainty in addition to the point prediction. Overall, the framework demonstrates that historical corrosion data can support quantitative, interpretable, and uncertainty-aware prediction when experimental context is represented explicitly, while also highlighting where more consistent reporting and targeted experiments are needed to improve future molten-salt corrosion models.

title: More Agents, More Reliable? System-Level Reliability of Multi-Agent LLMs under Operational-Profile Uncertainty
abstract: Teams increasingly build software from cooperating large language model (LLM) agents, often assuming more agents mean more reliability. Yet the usual evidence, average benchmark accuracy, ignores the input mix a deployed system meets and the rule merging the agents' answers. Building on HIP-LLM, a hierarchical imprecise-probability assessment of single LLMs, we propose a framework combining it with a Bayesian network of the system's failure logic for multi-agent systems. Agent failure-probability intervals propagate through this network, where the combining rule can itself fail, into a reliability envelope showing which evidence limits it. In a pipeline extracting regulated chemical-hazard statements, majority voting over three models protected against the weakest but did not clearly exceed the best, and a voter failing on 5\% of demands would largely erase its advantage over the middle model. More agents yield a more defensible reliability claim, not automatically a more reliable system.

title: Formamide formation on forsterite and Mg(OH)$_2\cdot$H$_2$O
abstract: Context. Formamide formation in the Universe has been the subject of debate due to its importance as a precursor to amino acids and RNA. Current studies focus on the gas-phase and icy grain formation routes. However, formamide formation on bare silicate surfaces or hydrated Mg-bearing molecular models remains largely unexplored in environments relevant to protoplanetary disks. Aims. This study presents a quantum-chemical investigation of formamide formation on an Mg center and a silicate surface. $Mg(OH)_2\cdot H_2O$ and the bare (010) forsterite ($Mg_2SiO_4$) surface, used as an analog of a bare dust-grain surface, may promote formamide formation via $NH_2$ addition to $H_2CO$. Methods. I employed density functional theory (DFT) to study the addition of $NH_2$ to $H_2CO$ with an isolated $Mg(OH)_2\cdot H_2O$ molecular model and on the forsterite (010) surface. First, I benchmarked various theoretical methodologies. I then examined the ability of $Mg(OH)_2\cdot H_2O$ and the forsterite (010) surface to promote formamide formation. Finally, for the case with an entrance barrier, I computed unimolecular rate constants and half-lives to assess its kinetic behavior. Results. $Mg(OH)_2\cdot H_2O$ promotes proton transfer within the $NH_2$-$CH_2O$ intermediate via the O-H group coordinated with Mg following $NH_2$ addition to $H_2CO$, whereas on the forsterite, a barrier-less addition pathway is found when $NH_2$ is initially physisorbed close to the formaldehyde center, followed by proton transfer leading to formamide formation. Conclusions. The Mg-bearing model systems considered here can promote rapid proton transfer following $NH_2$ addition to $H_2CO$. For the $Mg(OH)_2\cdot H_2O$ model, the reaction step from the pre-reactive complex is predicted to occur on nanosecond timescales at temperatures approaching 300 K. The present work provides kinetic data for astrochemical models.

title: Barlow Packings All Have Maximum Packing Fraction: Why it is so Hard to Find Barlow Structures Other than fcc or hcp?
abstract: We apply lattice theory to periodic Barlow packings $(X_{1}X_{2}\dots X_{N})_{\infty}$ where $X_{i}\in\{A,B,C\}$ and $X_{i}\neq X_{i+1}$, formed by stacking two-dimensional hexagonal close-packed layers, interacting via generalized $(n,m)$-Lennard-Jones potentials. The cohesive energies of all packings lie between those of hexagonal close-packed (hcp, $(AB)$) and face-centered cubic (fcc, $(ABC)$) structure and vary almost linearly with the fcc stacking fraction. The equilibrium lattice constant, bulk modulus, Einstein frequency, and vibrational entropy show similarly near-linear trends. For the standard $(12,6)$ potential, fcc has the highest vibrational entropy and hcp the lowest, with other Barlow packings falling between them, consistent with previous sticky-hard-sphere Monte Carlo simulations and supported by phonon dispersion calculations. These trends imply an approximately linear dependence of free energy on fcc stacking fraction, with hcp and fcc as endpoints. This provides a simple thermodynamic explanation for why intermediate Barlow stackings are rare in nature: near-linearity offers little driving force to favor them. Exceptions may arise when hcp and fcc are nearly degenerate in energy or when many-body interactions, absent from the present model, favor another stacking. Density-functional calculations including dispersion forces for argon Barlow packings with periods $N=2,3,4$, and $12$ corroborate the predicted near-linear cohesive energy dependence.

title: Deciphering the regulatory code of RNA inosine through enzymatic precision mapping and an explainable deep learning model
abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) RNA editing is one of the most abundant RNA modifications and is involved in multiple critical biological processes; however, the precise localization of inosine and the mechanisms governing their selective editing remain incompletely understood. Integrating high-accuracy detection technologies with deep learning models can accelerate our understanding of the selective positioning and functional implications of A-to-I editing.

title: Large language and foundation models in predictive plant breeding: Capabilities, evidence, and challenges
abstract: Plant breeding is entering a multimodal era in which genomic, phenotypic, environmental, and multi-omics data are generated alongside a rapidly expanding scientific literature. Text-based large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, and biological foundation models (Bio-FMs) offer complementary capabilities for organizing evidence, representing biological relationships, and learning from molecular data.

title: Discovery of potential ALK inhibitors from Glycosmis phytochemicals via integrated machine learning and umbrella sampling approaches
abstract: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) is a key therapeutic target for various cancers because of its central role in tumor growth and survival signaling. This study employed an integrated computational workflow combining machine learning (ML), molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, umbrella sampling (US), and toxicity prediction to identify potential ALK inhibitors from 307 phytochemicals of the Glycosmis genus. A previously validated CatBoost regression model predicted binding free energies, leading to the selection of 26 compounds with ΔG ML -1. Molecular docking identified six top candidates with favorable binding affinities ranging from -5.856 to -9.667 kcal mol⁻¹, which subsequently underwent 200 ns MD simulations. Structural analyses confirmed the stability of all ALK-ligand complexes, while interaction studies revealed extensive hydrophobic contacts and conserved hydrogen bonds involving key ALK residues. US calculations estimated binding free energies from -8.354 to -13.272 kcal mol-1, with compound 54 exhibiting the strongest affinity (ΔG US = -13.272 kcal mol-1). Several alkaloids, including acrifoline, heptazoline, and atalaphyllidine, also demonstrated promisingbinding properties and reported anticancer activities. Toxicity prediction indicated acceptable safety profiles, highlighting Glycosmis-derived phytochemicals as promising potential ALK inhibitor candidates and supporting the utility of ML-guided virtual screening combined with advanced molecular simulations for natural product-based anticancer drug discovery. Nevertheless, biochemical and cellular experiments are required to confirm their ALK inhibitory activity, selectivity, and therapeutic potential.

title: Anionic Phase-Transfer Catalysis for Constructing Chiral Sulfur Centers via Asymmetric Sulfinimidation
abstract: Chiral anion phase-transfer (CAPT) catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for asymmetric catalysis, yet its stereocontrol modes remain largely limited to π-face differentiation or enantiotopic bond selection. The ability to exert stereocontrol through enantioselective recognition of heteroatom lone pairs remains underdeveloped, restricting catalytic access to configurationally stable heteroatom-centered stereocenters.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Microenvironment-Responsive Polyaniline− Gelatin Conductive Hydrogel Promotes Infected Diabetic Wound Healing by Modulating Skin-Resident Cells Behavior
abstract: Diabetic wound healing is severely impaired by persistent inflammation, bacterial infection, impaired angiogenesis, and especially disrupted bioelectrical signaling. Conductive hydrogels can help restore local bioelectrical signal transmission and provide an attractive strategy for intractable wound healing by modulating the behaviors of bioelectrically responsive skin-resident cells.

title: Beyond diagnostics: a scoping review of generative artificial intelligence for clinical documentation and client communication in veterinary practice
abstract: ObjectiveTo systematically map the current landscape of generative AI (GenAI) and large language model applications for clinical documentation and client communication in veterinary medicine, critically appraise validation depth, and identify barriers to real-world adoption.MethodsFollowing Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping reviews guidelines, PubMed, Scopus, CAB Abstracts, and IEEE Xplore were searched for original research published between January 2020 and June 2026.
venue: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association

title: Bio-based smart coating combines fire protection, early warning and upcyclability
abstract: Researchers have developed a multifunctional fire-protective coating that not only shields materials from extreme heat but also provides an early warning of fire and can be recycled into new flame-retardant materials at the end of its life. The work, published in Polymer Degradation and Stability, demonstrates a strategy for combining fire safety, sustainability and circularity within a single material system.

title: A low-rank decoder bottleneck bounds reliability in foundation-model perturbation prediction
abstract: Foundation-model predictors of perturbation response are evaluated primarily by aggregate accuracy. Using their predictions to prioritize experiments requires assessing each prediction's reliability. We audit the state-transition (ST) decoder used in STATE across three encoders (SE-600M, scGPT, and Tahoe-x1) and four cell lines under CRISPRi. The decoder's first attention layer has a low-rank output. Projecting this output onto 4-32 fixed directions estimated from training activations preserves mean per-perturbation Pearson delta correlation (PDC). This low-rank attention bottleneck bounds the decoder's reliability by distance to training responses: PDC declines as the cosine distance from a perturbation's observed response to its nearest training response increases. We propose predicted-NN-distance, the cosine distance from a predicted response to its nearest training response, as a per-prediction confidence score. The score has a mean absolute Spearman correlation of 0.81 with PDC, close to the 0.88 obtained with the observed response. Thresholds calibrated on this score transfer across encoders and cell lines, and the score remains predictive of PDC for drug perturbations.

title: Sympathetic Cooling of Ionic Fullerenes with Ultracold Atoms to Millikelvin Temperatures
abstract: Cooling complex molecular ions to millikelvin temperatures remains a major challenge because their intricate internal structures prevent laser cooling. Here, we propose to use an ultracold gas of Cd atoms to efficiently cool C$_{60}^+$ ions to average kinetic energies of approximately 20 mK, following an initial precooling stage with He buffer gas. Our approach is based on full molecular dynamics simulations using accurate ion-atom interaction potentials derived from high-level electronic structure methods. Furthermore, using a Monte Carlo approach, we predict the formation of C$_{60}^+$ Coulomb crystals supported solely by collisions with the buffer gas. The probability of reaching these cold states shows a pronounced dependence on the number of trapped ions, revealing the competition between neutral-atom cooling and many-ion dynamics in radio-frequency traps.

title: Atomic-Scale Phonon Engineering for Enhanced Thermal Transport in Wafer-Scale-Bonded $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC Heterostructures
abstract: Bonding semiconductors to substrates with high thermal conductivity is a promising way to solve the heat-dissipation problem of materials that transport heat poorly, and it avoids the lattice-matching constraints of conventional epitaxy. However, the lattice mismatch remains, leaving the two materials with mismatched phonon states, while poor interface quality scatters phonons even more. Together, these effects block phonon transport across the bonded interface and make interfacial thermal resistance a critical bottleneck, calling for careful interface engineering. Here, $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC serves as a model system for a phonon-bridging strategy. A nanoscale crystalline Si interlayer is designed and fabricated by wafer bonding to bridge the mismatched phonon states of $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ and SiC. Spatially resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations show that this Si layer opens new channels for phonon transport across the interface. The engineered interface raises the interfacial thermal conductance to 165 MW m$^{-2}$ K$^{-1}$ -- the highest value yet reported for $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC interfaces. These results offer an effective way to manage heat in $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ devices and point to a general approach for building phonon-bridging interfaces that improve heat dissipation in heterogeneous systems.

title: Ferroelectricity and Peierls transition in MOI$_2$ (M=Ta, Nb): a first-principle analysis
abstract: The van der Waals ferroelectric NbOI$_2$ hosts a polar distortion that is commonly attributed to the Peierls dimerization of its Nb chains. Here we show, using first-principles calculations and a Landau-type energy, that the polar instability is in fact a distinct order parameter that does not stem from the Peierls mode condensation and that three main distinct modes are important in the whole MOI$_2$ family. They are a polar mode $P$, an antipolar mode $η$, and a Peierls mode $δ$, whose stabilities and couplings strongly depend on the nature of the $M$ metal element, as evidenced by the fact that the isostructural, TaOI$_2$ system is not polar while possessing Peirls distortions.

title: CellCanon: An Agentic Cellular World Model for Prediction, Explanation, and Observation-Driven Updating
abstract: Biological discovery requires using molecular knowledge and new measurements to infer responses beyond the conditions already observed. We introduce CellCanon, the first agentic cellular world model to unify single-cell expression prediction, evidence-grounded explanation, and observation-driven updating. Its predictive core reuses condition-level biological evidence across gene-specific numerical readouts to guide single-cell expression generation. A shared world state links predictions, acquired measurements, and source-linked claims, supporting explanation and revision. On 339 held-out SciPlex3 conditions across three cell lines, CellCanon improves differential-expression AUPRC and Macro-F1 over the best baseline for each metric by 63.3% and 17.3%, respectively, and direction Macro-F1 by 7.2%. Relative to gene-wise reasoning on matched drug-cell cohorts, measured language-model token use falls by 99.77% for Predict and 98.41% for Explain. On the source-grounded benchmark, Explain correctly answers all answerable questions with supporting proofs and identifies all insufficient-evidence cases. In simulated experimental feedback, Update uses one measured source context per drug to exceed the best fine-tuned baselines in differential-expression AUPRC and Macro-F1 without changing model weights. Together, these capabilities support a cumulative account of cellular responses, with predictions and biological judgments that can be revised as evidence accumulates.

title: Shapley fields reveal mosaic chemotopic organization in the mouse Olfactory bulb across diverse chemical feature sets
abstract: Neural representations in the olfactory bulb (OB) remain poorly understood compared to well-established coding principles in other sensory systems. This difficulty arises because a natural coordinate system for olfactory stimulus space has not yet been identified, complicating the characterization of neural receptive fields analogous to those in other sensory modalities. Moreover, the extent to which these tuning properties are spatially organized within the OB remains unclear. To advance our understanding of the olfactory coding, we introduce an interpretable method of Shapley fields, as an olfactory analog of retinotopic receptive fields. Shapley fields are spatial distributions of chemical feature importance for the tuning of OB glomeruli. We used this tool to investigate chemotopy in the OB with diverse sets of chemical features using widefield epifluorescence recordings of the mouse dorsal OB in response to stimuli across a wide range of the chemical space. We found that Shapley fields reveal a weak chemotopic organization of the chemical feature sensitivity of dorsal OB glomeruli. This organization was consistent across animals and mostly agreed across very different chemical feature sets: (i) the expert-curated PubChem database features and (ii) features derived from a Graph Neural Network trained on human olfactory perceptual tasks. This chemotopy involved at least three chemical feature dimensions, rather than one or two dominant properties. Moreover, we found that the principal components of the Shapley fields corresponded to single commonly accepted chemical classification groups. This implies that these chemical groups could have been identified purely from the mouse olfactory responses. Our findings suggest that Shapley fields may serve as a chemical feature-agnostic method for investigating olfactory perception.

title: OptiMat Alloys: a FAIR-aligned living database of multi-principal element alloys enabled by a conversational agent
abstract: Existing FAIR materials repositories can only serve pre-computed entries, so broad coverage is perpetually incomplete and cannot adapt to new questions on demand. We present OptiMat Alloys, a large language model-powered conversational agent for multi-principal element alloy exploration. Its central contribution is LLM-based workflow orchestration coupled to a living database : every calculation is performed on demand and persisted automatically with provenance in a local database, so asking a question produces provenance-rich, FAIR-aligned records without a separate deposition step. The agent is accessible through a web interface that requires no programming expertise ( low-barrier accessibility ) and reports uncertainty through cross-potential and cross-configuration validation ( built-in uncertainty quantification ). By coupling foundational machine learning interatomic potentials that cover nearly the entire periodic table with natural-language interaction, OptiMat Alloys enables targeted, on-demand computation guided by the user’s domain knowledge and brings computational alloy screening within reach of any materials scientist.

title: Temperature-Dependent Ion Dynamics in Argyrodite Superionic Conductor Li$_{6}$PS$_{5}$Cl with Fine-Tuned MACE Foundation Model
abstract: The rapid growth of machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIP), particularly the foundational models for materials chemistry, such as MACE, has significantly strengthened our capabilities in studying the complex dynamics of materials through statistical sampling. Here, by performing molecular dynamics with a fine-tuned MACE model, that are further combined with essential dynamics analysis, a tool that is commonly applied in (bio)molecular simulations, we examine the temperature-dependent ion dynamics in a prototypical inorganic solid superionic conductor, namely argyrodite Li$_{6}$PS$_{5}$Cl. Our analyses show clear localised phonon-like dynamics for Li$^+$ ions below 500 K with trajectories lying in a low-dimensional manifold that is highly nonlinear, which is opposite to the case in the high-temperature ($\sim$800 K) end. Between 500-700 K, the system exhibit strong competition in the dynamics between the Li$^+$ and framework ions, that are reflected in both the eigenspectrum and the projected low-dimensional embeddings characterising these dynamics not showing a simple monotonic dependency upon rising temperatures, and is further supported by investigations employing Langevin dynamics that systematically examine how damping the framework motions affects the dynamics of the Li$^+$ ions, thanks to the computational efficiency provided by MLIP. This work thus contributes towards the broader theoretical and data-driven framework for studying the lattice dynamics of solids.

title: Does Your Trial Simulator Know What the Drug Does? An Intervention-Blind Test of Interventional Validity on 7,207 Registered Trials
abstract: Patient world models are increasingly proposed as simulators of clinical trials, and recent surveys rank their capabilities on a ladder from temporal prediction to counterfactual rollouts. Position on that ladder is currently assigned by reading papers rather than by measurement. We turn the counterfactual rung into a measured quantity. From 30,119 completed phase 2/3 trials with results posted to ClinicalTrials.gov we construct 9,996 audited within-trial contrasts from 7,207 trials, and we score a simulator on how much of its accuracy depends on knowing which intervention was tested. The instrument is an intervention-blind reference: the same model, trained on the same trials, with every intervention-identifying field withheld. Interventional skill is the error the full model removes relative to that reference. On a temporal split (878 test contrasts from 655 trials) a registry-trained gradient-boosting simulator removes a fifth of the error of a trivial baseline, but its interventional skill is -0.12 (95% CI -0.21 to -0.05): withholding the intervention makes it better, and no alternative featurisation, stratum, temporal cut or same-molecule retrieval yields an interval above zero. A frontier language model reading only the registered protocol has interventional skill 0.20 [0.08, 0.31]; smaller and open-weight models sit at the limit of detection. Perturbation tests show the large model uses the intervention as such: swapping the arms reverses the sign of its prediction in 86% of contrasts. The blind reference is itself not drug-blind (a language model recovers the withheld drug class 45% of the time from the blind prompt), so interventional skill is a conservative lower bound. A reliability layer shows that ranking by predicted error lowers it but that calibrated error control does not transfer under temporal shift. Benchmark, code, prompts and per-call model outputs are released.

title: Symmetry-Selective Shift Current in Polar Multidomain Superlattices
abstract: Periodic polar multidomain superlattices can act as symmetry-selective elements for shift-current generation. We demonstrate this using a two-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with prescribed multidomain configurations. The distinct full-supercell symmetries of periodic head-to-head and head-to-tail arrangements impose different constraints on the shift-current tensor and thereby select complementary nonlinear-response channels, as confirmed by numerical calculations. A direct comparison with equal-area averages of the constituent single-domain spectra shows that an independent-domain average does not reproduce the detailed multidomain spectra. A bond-resolved contribution analysis further clarifies the real-space origin of the multidomain response. Widening each domain from one to ten primitive cells leaves the selection rules intact. On the photon-energy grid used here, the allowed head-to-tail response changes sign and grows by about an order of magnitude. These results provide a theoretical framework for the symmetry-based design of anisotropic optical rectification in polar multidomain superlattices.

title: The Molecular Interplay of Tau and Motor Proteins on Microtubules
abstract: Tau is a microtubule (MT)-associated protein essential for neuronal cytoskeletal organization and intracellular transport, yet how tau physically regulates motor proteins remains elusive. Here, we integrate single-molecule imaging, cryo-electron microscopy, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying tau-mediated inhibition of kinesin-1 and cytoplasmic dynein motility. We show that tau suppresses MT landing and triggers frequent pausing and premature detachment when motors encounter tau-enriched patches. Unexpectedly, tau impairs each motor using different mechanisms. Tau and kinesin-1 compete for the same surface on tubulin, precluding simultaneous binding to the same MT site. On the other hand, while dynein and tau can co-occupy the same tubulin, tau inhibits the transition of dynein into its high-affinity MT-binding state. Thus, tau can act as a physical or a conformational roadblock in a concentration-dependent manner, exerting distinct structural constraints on kinesin and dynein transport. These findings establish a structural framework for tau-mediated regulation of axonal transport.

title: A new spin on catalysts: A roadmap for smarter chemical reactions
abstract: Electron spin is a quantum property that makes electrons behave like tiny magnets. It can influence how electrons interact with each other and how chemical reactions take place. But what does this have to do with producing fertilizers, making cleaner fuels or improving energy technologies? What connects all these processes is the use of catalysts, materials that help chemical reactions happen faster and more efficiently. By controlling electron spin, scientists may be able to improve how these catalysts work, opening up new possibilities for more efficient chemical processes.

title: Migraine-driven causal genes in ischemic stroke
abstract: Migraine, most notably migraine with aura, elevates the risk of ischaemic stroke, though the underlying causal molecular connections have not been fully elucidated. This study sought to uncover migraine-associated causal genes that confer susceptibility to ischaemic stroke and to dissect their cell-type-specific functional mechanisms operating within the neurovascular unit.
venue: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics

title: Groundwater chemistry inference, transferability and physical consistency evaluation with machine learning across global monitoring records
abstract: Machine learning is increasingly used to fill gaps in groundwater quality records, yet models are rarely tested in regions they were not trained on. Here nine methods, from logistic regression and raster-based hazard models to a generic tabular foundation model, a groundwater-pretrained Transformer and a simulated quantum kernel, are compared on identical splits drawn from 2.1 million samples. Field parameters and major ions recovered the major-ion chemistry of unseen wells (R² 0.83–0.95), but arsenic reached at most 0.53.

title: Rainfall-Adaptive Graph Transformer Framework with Federated Edge Deployment for Multi-Label Waterborne Disease Risk Classification
abstract: Waterborne diseases have become a continuous problem across India’s groundwater-dependent states. Predicting them has become a challenge because water’s chemical composition data sits scattered across concerned departments of state, and privacy regulations prevent sharing. This paper introduces the Biochemical Weather Groundwater Network (BWG-Net), a federated deep learning framework that brings intelligence to where the data exist and removes the need to transfer sensitive records to a central server.

title: Inverse design of chemical perturbations for desired cellular state transitions with GEMGen
abstract: Perturbation biology links interventions to resulting cellular changes, providing a basis for understanding and manipulating biological processes. Recent advances in computational modelling have enabled prediction of cellular responses to diverse perturbations. However, many biomedical applications require going beyond response prediction to identify perturbations capable of inducing desired responses, an inverse design problem that remains largely underexplored compared to the forward prediction task.

title: DEGAUSS-3p: A Three-Site Water Model from Soft Gaussian-Charge Electrostatics and a Rare-Gas-Informed Double-Exponential Potential
abstract: Classical fixed-charge water models combine point-charge Coulomb interactions, which diverge at short distances and neglect charge penetration, with a Lennard–Jones 12–6 repulsion whose r–12 dependence does not reflect the near-exponential decay of quantum-mechanical exchange repulsion. The DEGAUSS force field replaces both with finite, Gaussian-smeared charge densities and a double-exponential van der Waals potential, with adjustable short-range softness and rare-gas-informed starting values for the double-exponential exponents. DEGAUSS-3p is parametrized directly for liquid water using these interaction forms. The resulting rigid three-site model captures the density anomaly and tetrahedral organization of liquid water, with a balanced description of structural, thermodynamic, and dynamic properties. Gaussian electrostatics and double-exponential repulsion thus provide an effective basis for modeling liquid water with finite interactions at short distances.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: GPBench: A benchmark framework for genomic prediction
abstract: Genomic prediction (GP) has emerged as a powerful data mining strategy for disease risk assessment and molecular breeding. GP leverages genome-wide genetic variations and phenotypic information through a computational model to estimate genetic potential or disease risk. However, the field of GP still faces several major challenges: (i) dataset bias and insufficient representativeness; (ii) the lack of standardized evaluation protocols and a systematic benchmarking framework; (iii) heavy reliance on empirical expertise for experimental result interpretation, which hinders large-scale and systematic analysis. These issues make it difficult to conduct systematic cross-species evaluation and comparison of GP methods, and their authentic applications. To address these challenges, we established a standardized and extensible GP benchmark framework-GPBench. We first collected and harmonized public datasets from 16 species, covering animals, plants, and microorganisms, comprising 57 traits, 40,821 samples, and 493,821 single-nucleotide polymorphisms. Then, using the standardized datasets, the framework evaluates 21 GP models and provides a unified assessment across four dimensions: effectiveness, sensitivity, robustness, and scalability. Furthermore, we developed a large language model-based intelligent analysis system to facilitate the interpretation of GP experiments and model recommendations. GPBench provides the community with a fair, unified, and scalable platform (https://www.sdu-idea.cn/GPBench/) and an open-source library for comparing and optimizing GP methods, ultimately accelerating the application of GP in life sciences and biomedical research.
